summary: Target-level plan of Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations, Part II: Witt vector cohomology of singular varieties. WV.0 builds Witt vector sheaves W_nO_X, WO_X and Witt ideal sheaves of schemes in characteristic p, with the tensor and isogeny rationalizations and Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology, and proves nil-invariance, invariance under finite universal homeomorphisms (with the connected-fibre criterion of Nakamura–Tanaka), Mayer–Vietoris, the higher-direct-image lemmas of Gongyo–Nakamura–Tanaka and finiteness with slopes in [0, 1). WV.1 proves Bhatt–Scholze's h-descent for RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] (Proposition 11.41, with the pushout gap E52 of their proof filled) and for RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p]. WV.2 constructs Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault's Witt vector cohomology with compact supports from the Witt ideal vanishing theorem and proves descent along proper hypercoverings. WV.3 constructs the morphism from rigid cohomology with compact supports and proves the Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault comparison with the slope < 1 part. WV.4 plans the Witt canonical system, pushforwards and Gros cycle classes on Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports and Chatzistamatiou–Rülling's action of proper correspondences. WV.5 plans quasi-resolutions, WO-rational and Witt-rational singularities, their independence of the quasi-resolution and Theorem 4.8.1 for CH_0-trivial fibrations. WV.6 derives the point-count congruences: ζ^{<1} = ζ^W, Ax–Katz modulo q, Serre's theta-divisor congruence, quasi-birational invariance for WO-rational singularities and Esnault's theorem with its singular extension. Imports: CrystallineCohomology CR.0/CR.4, rigid cohomology RD.4–RD.7, ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.1, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1/E2/E5, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0–SF.5, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.0/MC.2, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII PA.6. The Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin and Esnault–Groechenig routes are proposed as separate Part IIs (restructure).

nodes.title: Witt vector sheaves of a scheme in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and X a scheme with p·O_X = 0. For n ≥ 1, W_nO_X is the sheaf of rings U ↦ W_n(O_X(U)) (truncated p-typical Witt vectors of length n), and WO_X := lim_n W_nO_X is the sheaf U ↦ W(O_X(U)). For a quasi-coherent ideal I ⊂ O_X, W_nI := ker(W_nO_X → W_n(O_X/I)) is the subsheaf of Witt vectors all of whose components are sections of I, and WI := lim_n W_nI. These carry restriction R: W_{n+1} → W_n and Frobenius F: W_{n+1} → W_n (ring maps), Verschiebung V: W_n → W_{n+1} (additive) and the multiplicative Teichmüller map [−]: O_X → W_nO_X, with FV = p and V(x·F(y)) = V(x)·y, and exact sequences 0 → W_nI →(V) W_{n+1}I →(R^n) I → 0 of sheaves of abelian groups. The ringed space W_nX := (|X|, W_nO_X) is a scheme, with W_n(Spec A) = Spec W_n(A); W_nO_X and W_nI are quasi-coherent on W_nX, and W_n(V(I)) is the closed subscheme of W_nX cut out by W_nI. A morphism f: X → Y induces W_nf: W_nX → W_nY; if X, Y are of finite type over a perfect field k of characteristic p, then W_nX is of finite type over W_n(k), W_nf preserves being separated, of finite type and proper, and R^if_*(W_nI) = R^i(W_nf)_*(W_nI) as sheaves of abelian groups on |Y|. Finally RΓ(X, WI) ≅ Rlim_n RΓ(X, W_nI), and for X proper over k and I coherent, H^i(X, WI) = lim_n H^i(X, W_nI).
hypotheses: p is prime and p·O_X = 0; no reducedness or finiteness is assumed for the definitions.

Quasi-coherence of W_nI on W_nX and the Rlim formula need I quasi-coherent; the inverse-limit formula on cohomology needs X proper over a perfect field and I coherent (the groups H^i(X, W_nI) are then of finite length over W_n(k), so the tower is Mittag-Leffler).
W_nO_X is not an O_X-module for n ≥ 2: it is a sheaf of W_n(k)-algebras, and cohomology is sheaf cohomology of abelian groups on |X|.
proofSteps: Define W_nO_X on opens by the functor A ↦ W_n(A) = A^n (as sets); it is a sheaf because limits of sheaves of sets are computed objectwise and the ring structure is given by universal integral polynomials, so it is compatible with restriction (Mathlib's TruncatedWittVector and its ring structure).
The operator identities hold on sections by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-structural-identities; the exact sequences follow from the coordinate description of V as a shift and of R as truncation.

For X = Spec A, W_n(A_f) = W_n(A)_{[f]} (localization at the Teichmüller lift), so W_nX is a scheme covered by Spec W_n(A) for affine opens Spec A of X; quasi-coherence is the degree-zero case of CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-localization-descent (4), using W_rΩ⁰ = W_r (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/classical-de-rham-witt). W_nI is the kernel of a map of quasi-coherent W_nO_X-modules, W_n(O_X) → W_n(O_X/I), the structure sheaf of the closed subscheme W_n(V(I)).

If X is of finite type over k, W_n(A) is a finite W_n(A)-module extension of a finitely generated W_n(k)-algebra by induction on n (the kernel of R^{n−1} is V^{n−1}A, a finite module through F^{n−1}), giving finite type; properness and separatedness transfer because |W_nX| = |X| and W_nX → W_n(Y) is obtained from X → Y by nilpotent thickenings (CR12 §1.1).

The Rlim formula, in the enhanced derived category of sheaves of abelian groups (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category): each W_nI has vanishing cohomology on affine opens of a quasi-compact separated X and the transition maps W_{n+1}I → W_nI are surjective on affine opens, so the tower is Rlim-acyclic (WV.0/witt-limit-lemmas). For X proper the H^i(X, W_nI) are W_n(k)-modules of finite length, so the tower is Mittag-Leffler and lim¹ vanishes (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/mittag-leffler-lim-one).
acceptance: W_n(Spec F_p) = Spec ℤ/p^n and WO(Spec F_p) has global sections ℤ_p.
For X of finite type over k and I = 0, W_nI = 0; for I = O_X, W_nI = W_nO_X.

nodes.title: Rational Witt sheaves: tensor and isogeny conventions
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme with p·O_X = 0 and Sh(X) its abelian category of sheaves of abelian groups. (a) The tensor convention (Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault): WI_K := WI ⊗_ℤ ℚ (sheafified), with R^if_*(WI_K) = R^if_*(WI) ⊗ ℚ on noetherian spaces. (b) The isogeny convention (Chatzistamatiou–Rülling): let T(X) ⊂ Sh(X) be the full subcategory of sheaves killed by some nonzero integer; it is a Serre class, and Sh(X)_ℚ := Sh(X)/T(X) is the Serre localization, an abelian category with exact localization q: Sh(X) → Sh(X)_ℚ; write F_ℚ := q(F). Every left-exact f_* with enough acyclics induces Rf_*: D⁺(Sh(X)_ℚ) → D⁺(Sh(Y)_ℚ) with Rf_* ∘ q = q ∘ Rf_*. Thus R^if_*(WI_ℚ) = 0 means that some p^N kills R^if_*(WI), and an isomorphism F_ℚ ≅ G_ℚ induced by a map means that its kernel and cokernel are killed by a power of p. The two conventions agree on cohomology of proper schemes over a perfect field: for Z proper over k, H^i(Z, WO_{Z,ℚ}) = 0 if and only if H^i(Z, WO_Z) ⊗ ℚ = 0.
hypotheses: X is noetherian whenever the tensor convention is used for higher direct images (cohomology commutes with ⊗ℚ on noetherian spaces).

Statements of WO-rationality (WV.5) use the isogeny convention; statements with K = Frac W(k) coefficients (WV.2, WV.3, WV.6) use the tensor convention; the comparison for proper schemes is part of this node.
proofSteps: T(X) contains 0 and is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions (if p^a kills F′ and p^b kills F″ then p^{a+b} kills F), so it is a Serre class (Mathlib's ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass), and the localization at the morphisms that are isomorphisms modulo T(X) is abelian (Mathlib's SerreClassLocalization.abelian), with q exact and q(F) = 0 iff F ∈ T(X) (SerreClassLocalization.isZero_obj_iff).

Derived functors: CR12 Proposition 3.7.7 shows that a left-exact functor with enough acyclic objects induces a left-exact functor on the quotients whose derived functor commutes with q; apply it to Γ, f_* and lim.

Comparison for proper Z: H^i(Z, WO_Z) is a finitely generated module over the Dieudonné ring W_σ[[V]] (WV.0/witt-finiteness-slopes), so its torsion is killed by a single power of p; hence vanishing after ⊗ℚ is equivalent to being killed by p^N (GNT Remark 2.17 (5)).
acceptance: For the constant sheaf ⊕_{n≥1} ℤ/p^n on a point, the tensor rationalization is 0 but the isogeny rationalization is not.
For f proper and I coherent, R^if_*(WI)_ℚ ≅ (R^if_*(WI))_ℚ (GNT Remark 2.17 (2)).

nodes.title: Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a qcqs scheme with p·O_X = 0. The Witt Frobenius F: WO_X → WO_X is a ring endomorphism; W(O_X)[1/F] := colim(WO_X →F WO_X →F ⋯) is the sequential colimit sheaf, and the Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology is RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] := colim(RΓ(X, WO_X) →F RΓ(X, WO_X) →F ⋯), which agrees with RΓ(X, W(O_X)[1/F]) for qcqs X. Since FV = VF = p, F becomes invertible after inverting p, so RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p] = (RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F])[1/p]. The construction is contravariant in X and takes values in coconnective ℤ-module spectra (complexes concentrated in degrees ≥ 0).
hypotheses: X qcqs, so cohomology commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves.
F here is the Witt-vector Frobenius on coefficients, induced by the absolute Frobenius of X.
proofSteps: The colimit is a sequential colimit of sheaves of rings; for qcqs X sheaf cohomology commutes with filtered colimits, giving RΓ(X, W(O_X)[1/F]) = RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F].

nodes.title: Rational Witt sheaves are insensitive to nilpotents and radicals
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a perfect field k of characteristic p. (i) WO_X → WO_{X_red} induces isomorphisms WO_{X,K} ≅ WO_{X_red,K} and WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ WO_{X_red,ℚ}, compatibly with F and V, hence H^*(X, WO_{X,K}) ≅ H^*(X_red, WO_{X_red,K}). (ii) If I, J ⊂ O_X are coherent ideals with √I = √J, then WI_K = WJ_K and WI_ℚ = WJ_ℚ inside WO_{X,K} (resp. WO_{X,ℚ}); in particular W(I^a)_ℚ = WI_ℚ for all a ≥ 1. (iii) After inverting F instead, W(O_X)[1/F] → W(O_{X_red})[1/F] is an isomorphism for every scheme X with p = 0 whose nilradical is nilpotent (for instance X noetherian, as in WV.1); for an unbounded nilradical it can fail.
hypotheses: Finite type over a perfect field (for (i), (ii)); (iii) needs a nilpotent nilradical, not only a locally nilpotent one.
The isogeny version of (i) and (ii) needs the nilradical to be nilpotent (true for noetherian X): a uniform power of F then kills W(N).
proofSteps: Let N be the nilradical; on a noetherian X, N^{p^c} = 0 for some c. F acts on W(N) by raising every component to the p-th power, so F^c kills W(N) (a single power, uniformly).
Since FV = VF = p, p^c = V^cF^c kills W(N); so W(N) is bounded torsion, W(N)_K = 0 and W(N)_ℚ = 0. The exact sequence 0 → W(N) → WO_X → WO_{X_red} → 0 gives (i).
(ii): apply (i) to O_X/I and O_X/J and compare with O_X/(I+J) and O_X/(I∩J), whose reductions coincide; W(I^a) ⊂ W(I) with quotient W(I/I^a)-type subquotient killed by a power of F.

(iii): filtered colimits are exact, so 0 → W(N)[1/F] → W(O)[1/F] → W(O_red)[1/F] → 0 is exact; if N^m = 0 and p^c ≥ m then every section of N has vanishing p^c-th power, so F^c kills W(N) and W(N)[1/F] = 0.
acceptance: For X = Spec k[ε]/(ε²), W(k[ε]/(ε²)) ≠ W(k) but H^0(X, WO_{X,K}) = K = H^0(Spec k, WO_K).
For the double line X = Spec k[x, y]/(y²) ⊂ A², H^0(X, WO_X)_K = W(k[x])_K, the value for its reduction A¹.

For A = F_p[t_1, t_2, …]/(t_i^{p^i}), the Witt vector (t_1, t_2, …) lies in W(N) but is not killed by any power of F, so W(A)[1/F] → W(A_red)[1/F] is not injective: (iii) needs a nilpotent nilradical.

sources.match: W O_{X,K} is unchanged by passing to X_red, and WI_K depends only on the radical of I; the proof kills W(N)_K using that F is nilpotent on W(N) and FV = p.
W(I^a)_ℚ → W(I)_ℚ is an isomorphism, with the same proof as BBE Proposition 2.1 (ii).
For ideals with the same radical, WI_ℚ = WJ_ℚ, and WO_{X,ℚ} = j_*WO_{X_red,ℚ}.

nodes.title: Frobenius-inverted and rational Witt cohomology under finite universal homeomorphisms
nodes.statement: (i) Let f: X → Y be a finite, finitely presented universal homeomorphism of qcqs F_p-schemes. Then f* : RΓ(Y, WO_Y)[1/F] → RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] is an isomorphism; in particular (with p inverted) RΓ(Y, WO_Y)[1/p] ≅ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p]. (ii) For a proper surjective f: X → Y between separated finite type schemes over a perfect field k, whose fibres are connected after every base change to a field point (X ×_Y Spec L connected or empty for all Spec L → Y). Then WO_{Y,ℚ} → f_*WO_{X,ℚ} is an isomorphism; conversely, if WO_{Y,ℚ} → f_*WO_{X,ℚ} is an isomorphism, then the fibres of f are connected in this sense. (iii) In particular a finite universal homeomorphism f satisfies WO_{Y,ℚ} ≅ f_*WO_{X,ℚ} = Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ}.
hypotheses: (i): finite and finitely presented; Y qcqs.

(ii): 'connected fibres' means connected after base change to every field-valued point (Nakamura–Tanaka's convention); topological connectedness of fibres at points is not enough (see the acceptance test).
(iii): f finite, so R^if_* = 0 for i > 0 on quasi-coherent W_n-sheaves.
proofSteps: (i): By SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/frobenius-factors-through-universal-homeomorphism there are N and g: Y → X with f∘g = F_Y^N and g∘f = F_X^N; since F_X^N, F_Y^N act invertibly on Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology, f* is an isomorphism with inverse (F^N)^{−1}∘g*.

(ii) ⇒: Stein factorization (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/stein-factorization) reduces to f finite with geometrically connected (one-point, purely inseparable residue field) fibres, i.e. a finite universal homeomorphism; by WV.0/witt-nil-invariance reduce to X, Y reduced and affine, X = Spec B, Y = Spec A with A ⊂ B and B^{p^e} ⊂ A (Kollár); then p^e·W(B) ⊂ W(A), so W(A)_ℚ → W(B)_ℚ is an isomorphism.

(ii) ⇐: after Stein factorization f is finite with W(A)_ℚ ≅ W(B)_ℚ; reducing modulo a maximal ideal m of A shows W(A/m)_ℚ → W(B/mB)_ℚ is surjective, and W(A/m)_ℚ is a field, so B/mB has a single point n and the finite extension of complete discrete valuation rings W(A/m) → W(B/n) is bijective, hence A/m = B/n.
(iii) is (ii) for finite f, together with the vanishing of R^if_* for finite morphisms.
acceptance: Spec F_{q²} → Spec F_q is finite surjective with connected fibre but W(F_q)_ℚ → W(F_{q²})_ℚ is not an isomorphism: its fibre is not geometrically connected.
The normalization of a cuspidal cubic is a finite universal homeomorphism, so the cusp and P¹ have the same rational Witt cohomology.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 11.41, first paragraph, p. 53
sources.match: A finite universal homeomorphism induces an isomorphism on the Frobenius-inverted Witt presheaf because a power of Frobenius factors through it; in particular nilimmersions are inverted.
For proper surjective f with geometrically connected fibres, WO_{Y,ℚ} → f_*WO_{X,ℚ} is an isomorphism, by Stein factorization and the inclusion B^{p^e} ⊂ A for a finite universal homeomorphism.

sources.match: Connected fibres (in the base-change sense of §2.1) is equivalent to WO_{Y,ℚ} ≅ f_*WO_{X,ℚ}; the converse is proved by reducing to a finite map and comparing residue fields through Witt vectors.
Uses NT20 Lemma 2.17 to identify f_*WO_{Y,ℚ} with WO_{Z,ℚ} for a contraction and to pass to the normalization of S, which is normal up to universal homeomorphism.

nodes.title: Mayer–Vietoris for rational Witt sheaves along closed covers
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a perfect field k and X_1, X_2 ⊂ X closed subschemes with X = X_1 ∪ X_2 set-theoretically, Z = X_1 ∩ X_2 the scheme-theoretic intersection. Then 0 → WO_{X,K} → WO_{X_1,K} ⊕ WO_{X_2,K} → WO_{Z,K} → 0 is exact, and so are its isogeny version and the version 0 → WI_{X,ℚ} → WI_{X_1,ℚ} ⊕ WI_{X_2,ℚ} → WI_{Z,ℚ} → 0 for the ideal sheaves inside an ambient V ⊃ X; this gives the long exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence of H^*(−, WO_K). More generally, for a closed cover X = X_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ X_r the Čech-type complex 0 → WO_{X,K} → ∏ WO_{X_i,K} → ∏ WO_{X_{ij},K} → ⋯ → WO_{X_{1…r},K} → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: Set-theoretic cover; intersections scheme-theoretic (any scheme structure gives the same rational sheaves by WV.0/witt-nil-invariance).
proofSteps: With I_1, I_2 the ideals of X_1, X_2, one has W(I_1 + I_2) = W(I_1) + W(I_2) and an exact sequence 0 → W(O/(I_1 ∩ I_2)) → W(O/I_1) ⊕ W(O/I_2) → W(O/(I_1+I_2)) → 0.
I_1 ∩ I_2 is nilpotent because X = X_1 ∪ X_2, so WO_{X,K} = W(O_X/(I_1 ∩ I_2))_K by WV.0/witt-nil-invariance.
The r-fold statement follows by induction on r, writing the complex as the cone of a map of the complexes for X_2 ∪ ⋯ ∪ X_r and for X_1 ∩ (X_2 ∪ ⋯ ∪ X_r) and using the case r = 2.
acceptance: For two lines meeting at a point in A², H^0 of WO_K of the union is the fibre product of W(k[x])_K and W(k[y])_K over K.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.2 and Corollary 2.3 with proofs, p. 8
sources.match: Exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence of WO_K for a closed cover by two closed subschemes, and the exactness of the associated Čech-type complex for r closed subschemes.
The isogeny versions for WO_ℚ and for the Witt ideal sheaves of closed subschemes of an ambient V.

nodes.title: Higher direct images of Witt ideal sheaves
nodes.statement: For k perfect, f: X → Y a morphism between separated k-schemes of finite type, and a coherent ideal I ⊂ O_X: (1) R^i lim_n (f_*W_nI) = 0 for i ≥ 1 and R^i lim_n (R^jf_*W_nI) = 0 for i ≥ 2, j ≥ 0; hence there are short exact sequences 0 → R¹lim_n R^{j−1}f_*(W_nI) → R^jf_*(WI) → lim_n R^jf_*(W_nI) → 0. (2) If R^if_*I = 0 for all i > 0 then R^if_*(WI) = 0 for all i > 0. (3) R^if_*(WI) = 0 for i > m := max_{y∈Y} dim f^{−1}(y). (4) If R^if_*(WI) = 0 then R^if_*(WI_ℚ) = 0.
hypotheses: Finite type over a perfect field, so W_nI is a quasi-coherent sheaf on the noetherian scheme W_nX and its higher direct images are quasi-coherent on W_nY.
proofSteps: (1) A tower of sheaves with vanishing higher cohomology on affine opens and surjective transition maps on affine opens is lim-acyclic (CR12 Lemma 1.5.1; surjective towers are Mittag-Leffler with vanishing lim¹, ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1/mittag-leffler-lim-one); R^jf_*(W_nI) = R^j(W_nf)_*(W_nI) is quasi-coherent on W_nY, and Γ(U, f_*W_{n+1}I) → Γ(U, f_*W_nI) is W_{n+1}(I(f^{−1}U)) → W_n(I(f^{−1}U)), surjective.
(2) Induction on n with 0 → I →(V^n) W_{n+1}I → W_nI → 0 gives R^if_*(W_nI) = 0 for all n; then Rf_*(WI) = Rlim Rf_*(W_nI) = lim f_*(W_nI) by (1).

(3) W_nI is quasi-coherent on W_nX, whose fibres over W_nY have dimension ≤ m, so R^if_*(W_nI) = 0 for i > m; the sequences of (1) give vanishing for j ≥ m + 2, and R^{m+1} reduces to surjectivity of R^mf_*(W_{n+1}I) → R^mf_*(W_nI), which follows from 0 → I → W_{n+1}I → W_nI → 0 and R^{m+1}f_*I = 0.
(4) is WV.0/rational-witt-sheaves (R^if_*(WI_ℚ) = (R^if_*WI)_ℚ).
acceptance: For a resolution f of a rational singularity, R^if_*O_X = 0 for i > 0 gives R^if_*WO_X = 0 and hence WO-rationality of the target (CrystallineCohomologyPartII:WV.5/rational-implies-witt-rational).

sources.match: Rlim-acyclicity of the towers f_*W_nI and R^jf_*W_nI, the transfer of higher-direct-image vanishing from I to WI, vanishing above the maximal fibre dimension, and the passage to the isogeny category.

nodes.title: Finiteness and slopes of Witt vector cohomology of proper schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a perfect field k of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = W[1/p]. For each i, M := H^i(X, WO_X) is a finitely generated module over the Dieudonné ring R = W_σ[[V]] (with aV = Vσ(a)), separated and complete for the V-adic topology, and H^i(X, WO_X)_K is a finite-dimensional K-vector space on which F (σ-semilinear) acts bijectively with all slopes in [0, 1). The torsion of H^i(X, WO_X) is killed by a single power of p.
hypotheses: X proper over a perfect field; no smoothness.
proofSteps: H^i(X, W_nO_X) are W_n(k)-modules of finite length, so H^i(X, WO_X) = lim_n H^i(X, W_nO_X) (WV.0/witt-sheaf); V makes M a V-adically separated complete R-module.
M/VM injects into H^i(X, O_X), which is finite-dimensional; so M is finitely generated over R and torsion as an R-module: there are nonzero a_1(V), …, a_r(V) ∈ R with ⊕ R/Ra_i(V) ↠ M.

Factor each a_i(V), after inverting p, as a unit times a monic V-polynomial b_i(V) = b_{i,0} + ⋯ + V^ℓ with p | b_{i,j} (a Weierstrass-type factorization in the noncommutative ring, built p-adically); then R/Rb_i(V) ≅ W^ℓ, giving finiteness of M_K.

M_K is a quotient of a finite W-module after inverting p, so F has slopes ≥ 0 (slopes in the sense of the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition, CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition); FV = VF = p gives slopes ≤ 1; topological nilpotence of V excludes slope 1.
acceptance: H^1(E, WO_E)_K is one-dimensional of slope 0 for an ordinary elliptic curve E and two-dimensional of slope 1/2 for a supersingular one (H^1(E, WO_E) is the Dieudonné module of the formal group of E, of height 1 resp. 2).
For X smooth proper, H^i(X, WO_X)_K is the slope-[0,1) part of H^i_crys(X/W)_K (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-slope-spectral-sequence).

sources.match: For proper X the spaces H^*(X, WO_X)_K are finite-dimensional with Frobenius slopes in [0, 1); the proof uses the module structure over W_σ[[V]], finiteness of M/VM and a factorization of the annihilating V-power series.
Uses finite generation over W_σ[[V]] to compare the tensor and isogeny conventions for proper Z.

nodes.title: Fppf descent for Witt vector cohomology
nodes.statement: On qcqs F_p-schemes, the presheaves X ↦ RΓ(X, W_nO_X) (n ≥ 1), X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X) and X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] satisfy fppf descent: for every fppf cover {U_i → X} with Čech nerve U_•, the map RΓ(X, −) → Tot RΓ(U_•, −) is an equivalence of coconnective spectra. In particular, for an fppf map A → B of F_p-algebras with Čech nerve B^•, W_n(A) → Tot W_n(B^•), W(A) → Tot W(B^•) and W(A)[1/F] → Tot W(B^•)[1/F] are equivalences.
hypotheses: qcqs F_p-schemes; values are coconnective (complexes in cohomological degrees ≥ 0).
proofSteps: For W_n: induction on n using 0 → F^{n−1}_*O →(V^{n−1}) W_nO → W_{n−1}O → 0, where the kernel is O_X viewed through the (n−1)-st Frobenius, a quasi-coherent sheaf, so fpqc descent for quasi-coherent cohomology applies (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent).
For W = lim W_n, exchange the limit over n with the totalization.

For [1/F]: the values are coconnective, so π_k of a totalization is computed by a finite partial totalization (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/bounded-totalization-colimits); hence totalization commutes with the sequential colimit inverting F, and it suffices to check descent on affines before inverting F.
acceptance: For the fppf cover Spec F_{p²} → Spec F_p, W(F_p) = ℤ_p is the equalizer of the two maps W(F_{p²}) ⇉ W(F_{p²} ⊗ F_{p²}).

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 11.41, second paragraph, p. 53
sources.match: Checks that the Frobenius-inverted Witt presheaf is an fppf sheaf: coconnectivity reduces to affines before inverting F, and exchanging limits reduces to W_n, an iterated extension of Frobenius-twisted copies of W_1.

nodes.title: Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology of derived self-products
nodes.statement: Let Y = Spec A be an affine F_p-scheme and f: X → Y, Z → Y morphisms with X, Z qcqs. Choose finite affine open covers; the derived fibre products X ×^L_Y X, Z ×^L_Y X, … are the Čech-glued systems of simplicial commutative F_p-algebras B ⊗^L_A B′ on the affine pieces. Then (a) RΓ(X ×^L_Y X′, O) ≅ RΓ(X, O) ⊗^L_{A} RΓ(X′, O) (derived base change for coherent cohomology over an affine base); (b) applying W(−)[1/F] termwise, RΓ(X ×^L_Y X′, W(O)[1/F]) ≅ RΓ(X ×_Y X′, W(O)[1/F]), the classical fibre product: Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology does not see the derived structure; (c) for any simplicial commutative F_p-algebra R, the cone of W(R) → W(π_0R) is killed by p, so with p inverted the derived structure is invisible already without inverting F.
hypotheses: Y affine, X, X′ qcqs over Y; derived tensor products of simplicial commutative rings.
Only the affine-local form is used: no general theory of derived schemes is planned here.
proofSteps: (a) Choose finite affine covers (hypercovers if X, X′ are not separated). The alternating Čech complexes are finite complexes, whose terms are the rings of the affine pieces Spec B, Spec B′ (no higher quasi-coherent cohomology on affines); the Čech complex of the product cover of X ×^L_Y X′ has terms B ⊗^L_A B′, and since ⊗^L_A is exact in each variable it commutes with these finite totalizations (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/presentability-and-derived-tensor). This is the derived base change used by Bhatt–Scholze for coherent cohomology over an affine base.

(b) On each affine piece, W(R)[1/F] ≅ W(π_0R)[1/F] for a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra R, because W(R) has underlying simplicial set R^ℕ with π_i(W(R)) = ∏ π_i(R) for i > 0, killed by F since Frobenius kills π_i(R) for i > 0 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/derived-witt-adapter, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/frobenius-and-perfection); π_0 of the affine derived product is the classical tensor product B ⊗_A B′. Glue along the Čech cover.
(c) is the p-nullhomotopy recorded with E5:animation/derived-witt-adapter, from VF = p.
acceptance: For A = k[t], B = B′ = A/(t), the derived tensor product has π_1 = k (Tor_1) but W(k[t]/(t) ⊗^L k[t]/(t))[1/F] = W(k)[1/F] = W(k).

sources.locator: Notation 11.42, Lemma 11.43 with proof, Remark 11.44, pp. 51–52
sources.match: Derived F_p-schemes via simplicial commutative rings; W(O_X)[1/F] of a derived scheme equals that of its classical truncation because F kills the higher homotopy of W(A); the cone of W(A) → W(π_0A) is killed by p.

sources.locator: proof of Lemma 11.45, case n = 2, p. 52
sources.match: Uses that coherent cohomology commutes with derived base change over an affine Y, then removes the derived structure after inverting F.

nodes.title: The finite pushout replacing a blowup square
nodes.statement: Let Y = Spec A be a noetherian affine F_p-scheme, J ⊂ A an ideal with Z = V(J), and π: X = Bl_J Y → Y the blowup with exceptional divisor E = V(JO_X), where JO_X = O_X(−E) is π-ample. After replacing J by a suitable power (thickening E and Z) one has H^i(X, O_X(−E)) = 0 for i > 0. Put B′ := H^0(X, O_X) ×_{H^0(E, O_E)} A/J and Y′ := Spec B′, with the maps X → Y′ and Z → Y′ induced by the projections. Then: (i) B′ is a finite A-algebra and Y′ → Y is a finite universal homeomorphism; (ii) B′ → A/J is surjective with kernel K = H^0(X, JO_X), KO_X = JO_X, and E = X ×_{Y′} Z; (iii) Y′ is the pushout X ⊔_E Z in ringed spaces; (iv) RΓ(Y′, O) → RΓ(X, O) ⊕ RΓ(Z, O) → RΓ(E, O) is a fibre sequence.
hypotheses: Y noetherian affine of characteristic p; J an ideal; the thickening is chosen with H^i(X, O_X(−E)) = 0 for i > 0 (Serre vanishing for the relatively ample O_X(−E)).
E → Z is proper but in general not finite, so the pushout is not a Ferrand pinching; the explicit B′ supplies it.
proofSteps: X = Bl_J Y is the blowup (blowups and modifications: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/modification-domination). Serre vanishing: O_X(−E) is π-ample, so H^i(X, O_X(−nE)) = 0 for i > 0 and n ≫ 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/ample-serre-vanishing); replace J by J^n.

(i) H^0(X, O_X) is finite over A (proper pushforward of coherent sheaves), hence so is B′. B′ → A/J is surjective with kernel K = H^0(X, JO_X); for s ∈ K, s^m ∈ H^0(X, J^mO_X), the image of J^m for m ≫ 0 (X = Bl_J Y), so K ⊂ √(JB′); and B′_j = A_j for j ∈ J. Thus Y′ → Y is bijective on points with trivial residue extensions, finite, hence a universal homeomorphism (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/universal-homeomorphism-criteria).
(ii) KO_X = JO_X because J ⊂ K ⊂ H^0(X, JO_X); hence E = X ×_{Y′} Z.

(iii) and (iv): H^0 of the square is left exact by construction of B′ and right exact because H^0(X, O_X) → H^0(E, O_E) is surjective (H^1(X, O_X(−E)) = 0); in positive degrees H^i(X, O_X) ≅ H^i(E, O_E) and Y′, Z are affine.
acceptance: When Z is a point of a surface Y, the construction recovers a finite universal homeomorphism Y′ → Y that is an isomorphism away from Z.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 11.41, third paragraph, p. 53
sources.match: Arranges X to be the blowup of Y along Z with H^i(X, O_X(−E)) = 0 and replaces Y by a pushout Y′ = X ⊔_E Z, asserted to be a finite universal homeomorphism over Y with a square Cartesian up to universal homeomorphisms; the existence of this pushout is not justified in the source (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E52), and this node supplies it as B′ = H^0(X, O_X) ×_{H^0(E, O_E)} A/J.

nodes.title: Excision for Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology along abstract blowup squares
nodes.statement: Let E → X, E → Z, X → Y, Z → Y be a Cartesian square of qcqs F_p-schemes with Y affine and i: Z → Y a constructible closed immersion, and assume RΓ(Y, O_Y) → RΓ(X, O_X) ⊕ RΓ(Z, O_Z) → RΓ(E, O_E) is a fibre sequence. For n ≥ 1 let X^{n/Y} be the n-fold fibre product of X over Y and E^{n/Y} = X^{n/Y} ×_Y Z (the n-fold fibre product of E over Z). Then RΓ(Y, W(O)[1/F]) → RΓ(X^{n/Y}, W(O)[1/F]) ⊕ RΓ(Z, W(O)[1/F]) → RΓ(E^{n/Y}, W(O)[1/F]) is a fibre sequence for every n ≥ 1. For n = 1 the sequence is already a fibre sequence before inverting F.
hypotheses: Y affine; Z → Y constructible closed immersion; the structure-sheaf fibre sequence is a hypothesis.
Fibre products X^{n/Y} are classical; derived fibre products appear only in the proof.
proofSteps: n = 1: W = Rlim W_m, and each W_m is an m-fold iterated extension of Frobenius-twisted copies of O, so the structure-sheaf fibre sequence gives the W-sequence.

n = 2: tensor the structure-sheaf sequence over RΓ(Y, O) with RΓ(X, O); by derived base change over the affine Y this is the structure-sheaf sequence of X ← X ×^L_Y X, Z ×^L_Y X ← E ×^L_Y X; apply the n = 1 argument and then remove the derived structure after inverting F (WV.1/affine-derived-self-products), and compare with the n = 1 sequence.
n ≥ 3: induction in the same way.
acceptance: For X → Y a closed cover Y = X ∪ Z (disjoint union X ⊔ Z → Y), the sequence is the Mayer–Vietoris sequence.

sources.match: Under a structure-sheaf fibre sequence for a Cartesian square over an affine Y with constructible closed Z, the Frobenius-inverted Witt sequence holds for every self-product X^{n/Y}; the proof goes through derived self-products and Lemma 11.43.

nodes.title: h-descent for Frobenius-inverted Witt vector cohomology
nodes.statement: Let S be a noetherian F_p-scheme of finite Krull dimension. The functor X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] on the category Sch^fp_S of finitely presented S-schemes is a sheaf of spectra for the h-topology: for every h-cover X → Y in Sch^fp_S with Čech nerve X^{•/Y}, RΓ(Y, WO)[1/F] ≅ Tot RΓ(X^{•/Y}, WO)[1/F].
hypotheses: S noetherian of finite Krull dimension; h-topology generated by finitely presented v-covers (ArcTopologyAndDescent:AT.1/h-site).
Correction carried: the pushout Y′ used in the inductive step is the finite universal homeomorphism of WV.1/witt-pushout (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E52).
proofSteps: Write F(X) = RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F]. F inverts finite universal homeomorphisms, in particular nilimmersions (WV.0/witt-universal-homeomorphism-invariance), and is an fppf sheaf (WV.1/witt-fppf-descent).

The h-descent criterion (ArcTopologyAndDescent:AT.1/h-descent-criterion: fppf descent plus pullback along abstract blowup squares) is not applied as a black box, because excision is needed for every self-product of the blowup; its proof is followed instead. Reduce, by Rydh refinement and the dévissage of Lemma 2.10 of BS17 (ArcTopologyAndDescent:AT.1/universal-descent, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/proper-surjection-inductive-level), to proper surjective X → Y with Y affine, and argue by induction on dim Y; dim Y = 0 is fppf descent.

In the inductive step arrange X → Y to be the blowup of Y along Z with dim Z < dim Y and, after thickening, H^i(X, O_X(−E)) = 0 for i > 0; replace Y by the pushout Y′ of WV.1/witt-pushout (F(Y) = F(Y′) and F(X^{•/Y}) = F(X^{•/Y′}) since Y′ → Y is a finite universal homeomorphism).

By induction F(Z) ≅ Tot F(E^{•/Z}); as in the proof of BS17 Theorem 2.9 it suffices that F(Y′) → F(X^{n/Y′}) ⊕ F(Z) → F(E^{n/Y′}) is a fibre sequence for every n, which is WV.1/witt-blowup-excision applied to the structure-sheaf fibre sequence of WV.1/witt-pushout (iv).
acceptance: For a closed cover Y = Y_1 ∪ Y_2, descent along Y_1 ⊔ Y_2 → Y recovers the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of WV.0/witt-closed-mayer-vietoris after inverting p.
For the normalization of a nodal curve, descent expresses F(Y) through the normalization and the two preimages of the node.

sources.match: States the h-sheaf property of X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F] on Sch^fp_S and proves it by fppf descent, induction on dim Y through blowups, a pushout replacement and Lemma 11.45, following the proof of Theorem 2.9.
The h-topology, the inductive level of proper surjections, the criterion for h-sheaves of spaces via fppf descent and abstract blowup squares, and the dévissage lemma for universal descent.

nodes.title: Rational Witt vector cohomology is an h-sheaf
nodes.statement: Let S be a noetherian F_p-scheme of finite Krull dimension. Then X ↦ RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p] is an h-sheaf of spectra on Sch^fp_S. In particular, for a proper surjective map f: X → Y of finite type k-schemes (k perfect) whose Čech nerve is X^{•/Y}, there is a convergent descent spectral sequence E_1^{a,b} = H^b(X^{a+1/Y}, WO)_K ⇒ H^{a+b}(Y, WO)_K.
hypotheses: S noetherian of finite Krull dimension.
proofSteps: F is invertible after inverting p (FV = VF = p), so RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/p] = (RΓ(X, WO_X)[1/F])[1/p] (WV.0/frobenius-inverted-witt).

Inverting p is a filtered colimit, which commutes with totalizations of uniformly coconnective cosimplicial spectra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/bounded-totalization-colimits); apply WV.1/frobenius-inverted-witt-h-descent.
For a k-scheme of finite type, cohomology commutes with ⊗ℚ (noetherian), giving the spectral sequence with K-coefficients.
acceptance: For f: X ⊔ Z → Y with X, Z the two branches of a nodal curve Y, descent gives the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of WV.0/witt-closed-mayer-vietoris.
Agreement with Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault's descent for proper hypercoverings (WV.2/witt-proper-hypercover-descent) in the range where both apply.

nodes.title: Vanishing of higher direct images of Witt ideal sheaves
nodes.statement: Let f: X′ → X be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over a perfect field k, I ⊂ O_X a coherent ideal, I′ = IO_{X′}, U = X ∖ V(I) and U′ = f^{−1}(U). (i) If R^qf_*O_{U′} = 0 on U for all q ≥ 1 (for instance if U′ → U is finite, or an isomorphism), then there is c ≥ 0 such that p^c kills R^qf_*(WI′) for every q ≥ 1; hence R^qf_*(WI′_ℚ) = 0 and R^qf_*(WI′_K) = 0 for q ≥ 1. (ii) If U′ → U is an isomorphism, then kernel and cokernel of WI → f_*(WI′) are killed by a power of p, so WI_K ≅ f_*(WI′_K) and RΓ(X, WI_K) ≅ RΓ(X′, WI′_K); the same holds in the isogeny convention. (iii) For every coherent ideal I_1 ⊂ O_{X′} with √I_1 = √I′, the conclusions of (i) hold for W(I_1).
hypotheses: f proper between finite type k-schemes; I coherent; only the vanishing of R^qf_*O over U is needed in (i).
In (i) the constant c is uniform in q: the isogeny-convention statement, which is stronger than ⊗ℚ-vanishing.
proofSteps: Ideals W_n^{r,s}(I) = {a ∈ W_n : a_0 ∈ I^r, a_i ∈ I^s (i ≥ 1)} for s ≤ pr, with exact sequences 0 → W_{n−1}(I^s) →(V) W_n^{r,s}(I) →(R^{n−1}) I^r → 0 (BBE Lemma 2.5), because the Witt addition polynomials restricted to Teichmüller-type vectors are homogeneous of degree p^i.

Uniform killing (BBE Lemma 2.7; CR12 Lemma 4.6.3): the R^qf_*(I′^r) are coherent (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/qcoh-higher-direct-images with properness), and ⊕_r R^qf_*(I′^r) is a finite graded module over ⊕_r I^r (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness), supported on V(I) because R^qf_*O vanishes over U; hence there is a with R^qf_*(I′^{r+a}) → R^qf_*(I′^r) zero, and induction on n with the sequences above and the diagram lemma (if two outer maps vanish the composite vanishes) gives the same for W_n(I′^r), uniformly in n.

Frobenius F maps W_n(I′^r) into W_n(I′^{pr}); choosing p^c > a, F^c acts by zero on R^qf_*(W_n(I′^r)) for all n and r ≥ 1, hence on lim_n and R¹lim_n of these, hence F^{2c} kills R^qf_*(WI′) by the sequences of WV.0/witt-limit-lemmas; since FV = p, p^{2c} kills it.

(ii): the same argument applied to the kernels and cokernels K_n^r, C_n^r of W_n(I^r) → f_*W_n(I′^r), which are supported on V(I) and form lim-acyclic towers; WV.0/witt-nil-invariance identifies W(I^r)_ℚ with WI_ℚ.
(iii) is WV.0/witt-nil-invariance (ii).
acceptance: For the blowup f: X′ = Bl_0 A² → A² and I the ideal of the origin, R¹f_*(WI′)_ℚ = 0 although R¹f_*(I′) need not vanish for a given power.
For U′ → U finite of degree 2 (a double cover branched along V(I)), R^qf_*(WI′_ℚ) = 0 for q ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Higher direct images of WO through the exceptional locus
nodes.statement: Over a perfect field k, let f: X → Y be proper with X, Y separated of finite type, Y_0 ⊂ Y a closed subset such that R^qf_*O_X = 0 over Y ∖ Y_0 for q ≥ 1 (for instance f an isomorphism over Y ∖ Y_0), and E = f^{−1}(Y_0) with any closed subscheme structure, u: E → X. Then 0 → WI_{E,ℚ} → WO_{X,ℚ} → u_*WO_{E,ℚ} → 0 is exact and R^qf_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ R^q(f|_E)_*WO_{E,ℚ} for all q ≥ 1, compatibly with F and V. If moreover Y_0 = {s} is a closed point, then R^qf_*WO_{X,ℚ} is the skyscraper sheaf H^q(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) at s.
hypotheses: Proper f; the vanishing over Y ∖ Y_0 is a hypothesis; E with any scheme structure (WV.0/witt-nil-invariance).
proofSteps: W(O_X) → W(O_E) is surjective with kernel W(I_E), giving the exact sequence; R^qf_*(WI_{E,ℚ}) = 0 for q ≥ 1 by WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing applied to the ideal I_E, whose radical equals that of the pullback of the ideal of Y_0.
u is a closed immersion, so R^qf_*(u_*WO_E) = R^q(f|_E)_*WO_E; the long exact sequence gives the isomorphisms for q ≥ 1.
For Y_0 a closed point, sheaves supported at a closed point with closed image have vanishing higher pushforwards (GNT Lemma 2.25), and R^q(f|_E)_* computes H^q(E, −) at s.
acceptance: For a normal surface singularity with minimal resolution whose exceptional curve is a tree of smooth rational curves, R¹f_*WO_{X,ℚ} = H¹(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) = 0.

For the cone over an elliptic curve E, blown up at the vertex, R¹f_*WO_{X,ℚ} = H¹(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) is nonzero: one-dimensional of slope 0 if E is ordinary, two-dimensional of slope 1/2 if E is supersingular.

sources.match: For a projective birational f that is an isomorphism outside an isolated singular point, R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = H^i(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) as a skyscraper, compatibly with F and V, from the exact sequence of the ideal of E and Proposition 4.6.1.
For a divisorial contraction with exceptional divisor S, uses 0 → WI_{S,ℚ} → WO_{Y,ℚ} → u_*WO_{S,ℚ} → 0 and the vanishing of R^if_*WI_{S,ℚ} to identify R^if_*WO_{Y,ℚ} with R^i(f_S)_*WO_{S,ℚ}.

nodes.title: Witt vector cohomology with compact supports
nodes.statement: Fix k perfect of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = W[1/p], and a separated k-scheme U of finite type. Choose an open immersion U ⊂ X into a proper k-scheme (Nagata) and a coherent ideal I ⊂ O_X with V(I) = X ∖ U. Define RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}) := RΓ(X, WI_K) = RΓ(X, WI) ⊗ K and H^i_c(U, WO_{U,K}) its cohomology. Up to canonical isomorphism this is independent of X and I, and it carries a σ-semilinear Frobenius F and a σ^{−1}-semilinear V with FV = VF = p. It is contravariant for proper morphisms U′ → U, covariant for open immersions V ⊂ U, and for V ⊂ U open with closed complement T there is a distinguished triangle RΓ_c(V, WO_{V,K}) → RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}) → RΓ_c(T, WO_{T,K}) →^{+1}. There is a natural map RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}) → RΓ(U, WO_{U,K}), an isomorphism when U is proper.
hypotheses: U separated of finite type over a perfect field.
Independence uses the closure of U in X_1 ×_k X_2 for two compactifications and WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing (ii); the ideal I may be replaced by any ideal with the same radical.
proofSteps: Independence: for two compactifications X_1, X_2, the closure X of the diagonal image of U in X_1 × X_2 maps properly to both, isomorphically over U; WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing (ii) and WV.0/witt-nil-invariance give isomorphisms RΓ(X_i, WI_{i,K}) ≅ RΓ(X, WI_K), and the induced identifications satisfy the cocycle condition for three compactifications.

Functoriality: a proper U′ → U extends, after replacing X′ by the closure of the graph, to g: X′ → X with U′ = g^{−1}(U), and g* : RΓ(X, WI_K) → RΓ(X′, W(IO_{X′})_K) defines f*; an open immersion V ⊂ U gives W(J) ⊂ W(I) for the ideal J of X ∖ V.
The excision triangle is the cohomology of 0 → WJ → WI → W(I/J) → 0, where I/J is the ideal of Z ∖ T in the compactification Z = V(J) of T.
Existence of compactifications: Nagata (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4).
acceptance: H^*_c(A¹_k, WO_K) = 0, while H^0(A¹_k, WO_K) = W(k[t])_K is infinite-dimensional.
H^1_c(G_{m,k}, WO_K) = K and H^i_c(G_{m,k}, WO_K) = 0 for i ≠ 1.

nodes.title: Proper hypercoverings and simplicial resolutions by smooth schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a reduced separated k-scheme of finite type and N ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. An (N-truncated) proper hypercovering of X is an augmented (N-truncated) simplicial k-scheme f_•: X_• → X such that each X_n → (cosk_{n−1} sk_{n−1} X_•)_n is proper and surjective (0 ≤ n ≤ N); an étale hypercovering is defined with étale surjective maps. An (N-truncated) simplicial resolution is a proper hypercovering such that, for each n ≤ N, there is a dense open U_n ⊂ X over which sk_n X_• is an n-truncated étale hypercovering, and each X_n is a smooth quasi-projective k-scheme. Every reduced separated k-scheme of finite type has simplicial resolutions (and N-truncated ones whose N-coskeleton is a proper hypercovering).
hypotheses: k perfect (de Jong's alteration theorem is applied componentwise).
Coskeleta are taken over X in the category of separated k-schemes of finite type.
proofSteps: For each irreducible component, de Jong's theorem gives a smooth quasi-projective X′ with a projective surjective generically étale X′ → X (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem); apply it componentwise to obtain a map étale over a dense open.

Build the hypercovering inductively as in Deligne (Hodge III, (6.2.5)): at step n apply the alteration to (cosk_{n−1} sk_{n−1} X_•)_n; the class of proper surjective maps that are étale over a dense open of X satisfies the conditions for hypercoverings (Tsuzuki's (HC)). The rigid-cohomology roadmap builds proper hypercoverings with smooth terms in the same way (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/smooth-proper-hypercovering); here the terms are moreover quasi-projective and the coverings étale over dense opens.
acceptance: A smooth quasi-projective X is its own simplicial resolution (constant simplicial scheme).

nodes.title: Descent for Witt cohomology with compact supports along proper hypercoverings
nodes.statement: Let X be a reduced k-scheme of finite type, N ∈ ℕ, f_•: X_• → X an N-truncated proper hypercovering, I ⊂ O_X a coherent ideal with U = X ∖ V(I), and I_q = IO_{X_q}. Assume that the restriction U_• of X_• over U is an N-truncated étale hypercovering of U. Then the complex 0 → WI_K → f_{0*}(WI_{0,K}) → ⋯ → f_{N*}(WI_{N,K}), with WI_K in degree −1, is acyclic in degrees ≠ N, and the canonical maps H^q(X, WI_K) → H^q(X_•, WI_{•,K}) are isomorphisms for q < N. In particular, with X proper and U ⊂ X, H^q_c(U, WO_{U,K}) ≅ H^q_c(U_•, WO_{U_•,K}) for q < N.
hypotheses: U_• → U an N-truncated étale hypercovering; the comparison holds below degree N.
proofSteps: For the complexes L_n^{•,r}: 0 → W_n(I^r) → f_{0*}W_n(I_0^r) → ⋯, the direct sum over r of the n = 1 complexes is a complex of finite graded modules over ⊕ I^r (EGA III 3.3.1); over U it is acyclic in degrees < N by étale cohomological descent for quasi-coherent sheaves (bounded-below hypercover descent, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/bounded-below-hypercover-descent, for the étale topology, on which quasi-coherent sheaves satisfy descent, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent), so a power of I kills the cohomology and the transition maps H^{q,r+b} → H^{q,r} vanish for some b.

Induction on n with the ideals W_n^{r,r+b} of BBE Lemma 2.5 and the diagram lemma shows H^{q,r+2b}_n → H^{q,r}_n is zero, so a power of F kills H^q_n for r ≥ 1, hence on Rlim and the limit complex WI_• → in degrees < N; F becomes invertible after ⊗K, giving acyclicity.

Each f_q is proper and its restriction U_q → U is étale and proper, hence finite, so WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing (i) gives R^if_{q*}(WI_{q,K}) = 0 for i ≥ 1; thus f_{•*}WI_{•,K} computes Rf_{•*}WI_{•,K}, and (i) gives the statement on H^q.
acceptance: For the normalization P¹ → X of a nodal cubic (N = 1), H^0(X, WO_K) ≅ H^0 of the descent complex = K and H^1(X, WO_K) = K is read off from the two points over the node.

sources.match: For an N-truncated proper hypercovering étale over U, the augmented complex of Witt ideal sheaves with K-coefficients is acyclic below N and the Witt cohomology of X agrees with that of the simplicial scheme below degree N; the proof bounds Frobenius on graded cohomology with the ideals of Lemma 2.5.

nodes.title: Slope parts of F-isocrystals and of characteristic polynomials
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, K = W(k)[1/p] with Frobenius σ, and (E, F) an F-isocrystal: a finite-dimensional K-vector space with a σ-semilinear bijection F. For λ ∈ ℚ let E_λ ⊂ E be the slope-λ part: the unique F-stable subspace with K̄_0 ⊗_K E_λ equal to the isoclinic slope-λ summand given by Dieudonné–Manin over K̄_0 = W(k̄)[1/p] (it is Gal(k̄/k)-stable, so it descends). For ρ ∈ ℝ, E^{<ρ} := ⊕_{λ<ρ} E_λ. E ↦ E^{<ρ} is an exact functor and E = ⊕_λ E_λ. Over k = F_q (q = p^a) with φ = F^a linear, and v_q normalized by v_q(q) = 1, for P(t) ∈ 1 + tK[t] let P^λ be the product of the irreducible factors whose Newton polygon is a segment of slope λ (normalized P^λ(0) = 1) and P^{<ρ} = ∏_{λ<ρ} P^λ, extended multiplicatively to rational functions R with R(0) = 1. Then det(1 − tφ | E^{<ρ}) = det(1 − tφ | E)^{<ρ}.
hypotheses: k perfect; E finite-dimensional with F bijective.
Slopes are measured with v_p(p) = 1 for F and with v_q(q) = 1 for the linear φ = F^a; the two normalizations agree (slope of F = v_q of eigenvalues of φ).
proofSteps: Over k̄ the Dieudonné–Manin classification gives the canonical isoclinic decomposition and maps between different slopes vanish (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition); canonicity gives Galois stability and descent to K; exactness follows from the vanishing of Hom between different slopes.

Over F_q, the slopes are v_q of the eigenvalues of φ (Manin), so the characteristic polynomial factors through the Newton polygon (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal).
acceptance: For E = K with F = p^aσ (a ∈ ℤ), E^{<1} = E iff a ≤ 0.
For H² of P¹ (one-dimensional, F = pσ), E^{<1} = 0.

sources.match: Defines the slope-λ subspace through Dieudonné–Manin over W(k̄)[1/p] and Galois descent, and the slope < ρ subspace as the sum over λ < ρ; these are exact functors.
Defines P^λ and P^{<ρ} through Newton polygons with v_q(q) = 1 and records, by Manin's theorem, that the characteristic polynomial of φ on the slope < ρ part is the slope < ρ factor.

nodes.title: The Witt realization of overconvergent functions from a Frobenius lift
nodes.statement: Let P be a smooth separated formal W-scheme with special fibre P_0, X ⊂ P_0 a closed subscheme with ideal J ⊂ O_P (containing p), A_{X,P} := sp_*O_{]X[_P} the sheaf of analytic functions on the tube, and F: P → P a σ-semilinear lift of the absolute Frobenius of P_0. Then there is a ring homomorphism A_{X,P} → WO_{X,K}, functorial in (X, P, F), obtained as the composite of Berthelot's map A_{X,P} → P̂(J)_K into the p-adically completed divided power envelope with a compatible system of ring maps P(J_n) → W_nO_X, J_n = JO_{P_n}.
hypotheses: P smooth separated over W with a Frobenius lift F; X a closed subscheme of the special fibre.
Divided powers on J are compatible with the canonical divided powers of p.
proofSteps: Since O_P is p-torsion-free, F defines the Cartier–Dieudonné–Dwork section s_F: O_P → W(O_P) of the reduction, characterized by w_i(s_F(x)) = F^i(x) for all ghost components (for reduced targets this is CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-frobenius-lift-universal).

Composing with W(O_P) → W_n(O_X) gives O_{P_n} → W_nO_X sending J_n into V W_{n−1}O_X, which carries divided powers γ_m(Vx) = (p^{m−1}/m!)V(x^m) compatible with those of p (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-verschiebung-divided-powers); the universal property of the PD envelope (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-envelope) gives P(J_n) → W_nO_X, compatible in n.
P̂(J)/p^n = P(J_n), so the limit gives P̂(J) → WO_X; precompose with Berthelot's A_{X,P} → P̂(J)_K (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map) and invert p.
acceptance: For X = P_0 = Spec k and P = Spf W with F = σ, the map is the identity K → W(k)[1/p].
For X smooth with P a lift, composing with the augmentation recovers the map used for the crystalline–de Rham–Witt comparison.

nodes.title: The morphism from rigid cohomology with compact supports to Witt vector cohomology with compact supports
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, U a separated k-scheme of finite type. There is a morphism a_U: RΓ_{rig,c}(U/K) → RΓ_c(U, WO_{U,K}) in D^b(K), functorial in U for proper morphisms, constructed as follows: for X ⊃ U proper, Y = X ∖ U with coherent ideal I, and a closed immersion X ⊂ P into a smooth formal W-scheme, there are morphisms a_{X,P}: A_{X,P} ⊗ Ω^•_P → WO_{X,K} and a_{U,X,P}: (A_{X,P} ⊗ Ω^•_P → A_{Y,P} ⊗ Ω^•_P)_t → WI_K in D^b(X, K), equal to the composite with WV.3/frobenius-lift-witt-map when P carries a Frobenius lift, independent of the lift, and compatible with the canonical isomorphisms for two embeddings; in general they are defined through Čech covers by affine opens with liftable embeddings. Applying RΓ(X, −) gives a_U. Properties: (i) for X smooth proper, a_X is the composite RΓ_rig(X/K) ≅ RΓ_crys(X/W)_K ≅ RΓ(X, WΩ^•_X)_K → RΓ(X, WO_X)_K; (ii) a_U is compatible with passing to U_red; (iii) for V ⊂ U open with complement T, a_V, a_U, a_T form a morphism of excision triangles; (iv) a_U commutes with Frobenius.
hypotheses: U separated of finite type over a perfect field; embeddings of compactifications in smooth formal schemes exist locally (quasi-projective case globally, with Frobenius lift on an open of projective space).
proofSteps: A_{X,P} ⊗ Ω^•_P = sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P} computes rigid cohomology of proper X (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex). With a Frobenius lift, the ring map of WV.3/frobenius-lift-witt-map composed with the augmentation A_{X,P} ⊗ Ω^•_P → A_{X,P} gives a_{X,P,F}; for two lifted embeddings, the diagonal embedding into P × P′ with F × F′ and functoriality show the induced map in D^b(X, K) is the canonical isomorphism (4.1), so a_{X,P,F} is independent of F.
Without global lifts, cover X by affine opens X_i ⊂ P_i with lifts and use the Čech double complexes (4.10) and (4.11) on both sides.
For U ⊂ X, apply the construction to X and Y = X ∖ U and use that (WO_{X,K} → WO_{Y,K}) resolves WI_K; functoriality reduces, via WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing (ii), to U′ dense in X′.

(i): in the smooth lifted case the maps P(J_n) → W_nO_X are those of Illusie's crystalline–de Rham–Witt comparison, so the diagram with Berthelot's comparison (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism) and CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/crystalline-comparison commutes; (ii), (iii) by construction (BBE leaves them as exercises; the proof is the functoriality of the Čech construction).
acceptance: For U = Spec k, a_U is the identity of K.
For X = P¹, a_X is an isomorphism on H⁰ and the zero map H²_rig(P¹) = K(−1) → H²(P¹, WO_K) = 0.

nodes.title: Simplicial embeddings with Frobenius lifts
nodes.statement: Given a reduced separated finite type k-scheme X, a closed immersion X ⊂ P into a smooth formal W-scheme carrying a Frobenius lift F, and N ∈ ℕ: There are a proper hypercovering X_• → X, a P-augmented simplicial formal W-scheme P_• with a σ-semilinear Frobenius lift F_•, and a closed immersion of simplicial schemes X_• → P_• over X ⊂ P such that: (i) each X_n → P_n is a closed immersion and P_n → P commutes with the Frobenius lifts; (ii) sk_N X_• is an N-truncated simplicial resolution of X; (iii) X_• = cosk_N sk_N X_• and P_• = cosk_N sk_N P_•; (iv) each P_n is smooth over P and P_n → (cosk_{n−1} sk_{n−1} P_•)_n is smooth.
hypotheses: X reduced, separated, finite type; X ⊂ P with a Frobenius lift (for projective X, P is an open of a projective formal space with a lifted Frobenius).
proofSteps: Take an N-truncated simplicial resolution (WV.2/simplicial-resolution) and its N-coskeleton X_•.

Embed each quasi-projective X_m (m ≤ N) in a smooth formal W_m with Frobenius lift F_m; form Γ_n(W_m) = ∏_{γ: [m] → [n]} W_m with the induced simplicial structure and Frobenius ∏F_m, and P_• = P ×_W ∏_{m≤N} Γ_•(W_m).

The product of the embeddings indexed by γ gives X_• → P_•, a closed immersion in degrees ≤ N because one factor is the given embedding, and in all degrees by the coskeleton property; smoothness of the comparison maps P_n → (cosk_{n−1} sk_{n−1} P_•)_n is Tsuzuki's computation for such coskeletal products of smooth formal schemes (cited by BBE as [28, 7.3.3] and [10, 11.2.5]; those papers were not read), and the resulting (X_•, X_•, P_•) is a simplicial frame in the sense of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame.
acceptance: For X smooth projective with a lifted embedding, the constant simplicial objects satisfy the lemma.

sources.match: Constructs a proper hypercovering X_• with N-truncated simplicial resolution, a simplicial smooth formal scheme P_• with Frobenius lift and a closed immersion X_• → P_• over X ⊂ P with coskeletal and smoothness properties, following Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki.

nodes.title: Smooth proper case: slope < 1 rigid cohomology is Witt cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth proper k-scheme. For every q, a_X induces an isomorphism H^q_rig(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^q(X, WO_X)_K compatible with Frobenius, and H^q(a_X) is zero on the slope ≥ 1 part.
hypotheses: X smooth and proper over a perfect field k.
proofSteps: By WV.3/rigid-to-witt-morphism (i), a_X is the composite of the rigid–crystalline comparison (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison), the crystalline–de Rham–Witt comparison (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/crystalline-comparison) and the augmentation WΩ^•_X → WO_X; all are Frobenius-compatible.

The slope spectral sequence degenerates after ⊗K and identifies H^q(X, WO_X)_K with the slope-[0, 1) part of H^q_crys(X/W)_K, the augmentation being the projection to the zeroth column (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-slope-spectral-sequence).
acceptance: For an abelian variety A of dimension g and p-rank f, H¹(A, WO_A)_K has dimension f (the slope-0 part of H¹_crys).

sources.match: For proper smooth X the slope < 1 part of crystalline cohomology is H^*(X, WO_X)_K by the slope spectral sequence, and a_X induces this identification.
a_X is the composite of the comparison isomorphisms and the augmentation.

nodes.title: Witt vector cohomology computes the slope < 1 part of rigid cohomology
nodes.statement: Take k perfect of characteristic p, K = W(k)[1/p], and any separated k-scheme X of finite type. For every q the morphism a_X induces a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism b^q_X: H^q_{rig,c}(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^q_c(X, WO_{X,K}), functorial for proper maps and compatible with excision. In particular, for X proper, H^q_rig(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^q(X, WO_X) ⊗ K.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over a perfect field; no smoothness or properness.
proofSteps: H^q_{rig,c}(X/K) is finite-dimensional with bijective Frobenius (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology), so the slope < 1 part is defined and a_X induces b^q_X; the slope < 1 functor is exact.

Induction on d = dim X. By the reduction compatibility assume X reduced; dimension 0 is the smooth proper case (WV.3/smooth-proper-slope-identification). If the theorem holds below dimension d, excision triangles (WV.3/rigid-to-witt-morphism (iii)) and the five lemma show it for open subsets of smooth proper schemes of dimension d, and allow replacing X by any dense open neighbourhood of its generic points, hence by an irreducible affine U, hence by a projective compactification X̄.

For X̄ ⊂ P with Frobenius lift, take N ≥ 2d and the simplicial data of WV.3/simplicial-frobenius-embedding; on a dense open U the restriction U_• is an étale hypercovering. The Frobenius lift gives a morphism of descent spectral sequences E_1^{i,j} = H^j_{rig,c}(U_i/K)^{<1} ⇒ H^{i+j}_{rig,c}(U_•/K)^{<1} and E_1^{i,j} = H^j_c(U_i, WO_K) ⇒ H^{i+j}_c(U_•, WO_K), which is an isomorphism on E_1 for i ≤ N because each U_i is an open of a smooth projective X_i of dimension d.

The augmentations are isomorphisms in degrees ≤ N: on the rigid side by Tsuzuki's proper descent (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/proper-hypercover-descent-spectral-sequence, RD.5/cohomological-descent-for-proper-hypercoverings), on the Witt side by WV.2/witt-proper-hypercover-descent; both sides vanish above 2d (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension, WV.2/compact-support-finiteness).

nodes.title: Vanishing of compactly supported Witt cohomology of smooth affine varieties
nodes.statement: Suppose X is proper over a perfect field k and the complement U = X ∖ Y of the closed subscheme Y defined by a coherent ideal I is affine, smooth and equidimensional of dimension n. Then for every r ≥ 1 and every degree i ≠ n, the groups H^i(X, WI^r)_K — which coincide with H^i(X, WI)_K and with H^i_c(U, WO_{U,K}) — are zero.
hypotheses: U affine, smooth, equidimensional of dimension n; X proper; I any coherent ideal with V(I) = Y.
proofSteps: For U smooth affine, H^i_rig(U/K) is Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology, the cohomology of the de Rham complex of a dagger algebra of dimension n, which has no terms above degree n, so it vanishes for i > n (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-cohomology); Poincaré duality for smooth equidimensional U (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/poincare-duality) gives H^i_{rig,c}(U/K) = 0 for i < n, so WV.3/berthelot-bloch-esnault-comparison gives H^i_c(U, WO_K) = 0 for i < n.
For i > n: H^i_c(U, WO_K) does not change when X is replaced by the closure of U, of dimension n, and the cohomology of a scheme of dimension n vanishes above n (WV.2/compact-support-finiteness).
WI^r and WI have the same rationalization (WV.0/witt-nil-invariance).

nodes.title: The Witt canonical system and Ekedahl duality
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field and X a k-scheme of finite type of pure dimension d with structure map π: X → Spec k. For n ≥ 1 let K_{X,n} := W_n(π)^!(W_n(k)) be the dualizing complex of the W_n(k)-scheme W_nX (upper shriek of the finite type morphism W_nX → Spec W_n(k)); the K_{X,n} form a projective system (a Witt dualizing system) with Frobenius, Verschiebung and restriction. The Witt canonical system is W_nω_X := H^{−d}(K_{X,n}) and Wω_X := lim_n W_nω_X. Properties: (1) W_1ω_X is the canonical sheaf ω_X when X is normal; (2) K_{X,n} is concentrated in degrees [−d, 0], and W_nω_X[d] → K_{X,n} is a quasi-isomorphism when X is Cohen–Macaulay; (3) W_nω_X is a coherent S2 sheaf on W_nX; (4) for X smooth, W_•ω_X ≅ W_•Ω^d_X (Ekedahl), and W_•Ω^•_X is self-dual: the product pairing W_nΩ^i ⊗ W_nΩ^{d−i} → W_nΩ^d induces an isomorphism of the Cousin complex of W_•Ω_X with its dual (Ekedahl); (5) for a proper morphism f: X → Y between k-schemes of the same pure dimension there is a trace f_*: f_*W_•ω_X → W_•ω_Y, compatible with composition and localization; (6) 0 → W_{n−1}ω_X →(p) W_nω_X →(F^{n−1}) ω_X is exact, and right exact if X is CM.
hypotheses: k perfect; X of finite type and pure dimension d; duality for the finite type W_n(k)-schemes W_nX.
Ekedahl's theorems (smooth case) are used through the statements recorded in Chatzistamatiou–Rülling §1.10; Ekedahl's papers themselves were not read for this plan.
proofSteps: W_nX is of finite type over the artinian ring W_n(k) (WV.0/witt-sheaf), so it has the dualizing complex W_n(π)^!W_n(k) of coherent duality (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/scheme-dualizing, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/upper-shriek-compactification-independence).

Transition maps and F, V: duality for the finite morphisms i_n: W_{n−1}X → W_nX and the Frobenius-twisted closed immersion X → W_nX, applied to 0 → F^{n−1}_*O_X →(V^{n−1}) W_nO_X → W_{n−1}O_X → 0, gives the triangle i_{n*}K_{X,n−1} → K_{X,n} → (iF^{n−1})_*K_{X,1} → and hence (2) and (6) by induction on n.
The trace f_* is H^{−d} of the Grothendieck trace Rf_*K_{X,n} → K_{Y,n} for proper f (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/sheafified-grothendieck-duality).

For X smooth, Ekedahl's computation identifies K_{X,•} with the Cousin complex of W_•Ω^d_X[d], the top degree of the de Rham–Witt complex (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/classical-de-rham-witt), and the pairing on W_•Ω^•_X with the duality pairing (CR12 Corollaries 1.10.5–1.10.6).
acceptance: For X = Spec k, W_nω_X = W_n(k).
For X smooth of dimension d, W_1ω_X = Ω^d_X.

nodes.title: Pushforward on Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: Let S be a k-scheme. Let Sm*/S be the category of pairs (X, Φ) with X an S-scheme smooth over k and Φ a family of supports on X, morphisms f: (X, Φ) → (Y, Ψ) being S-morphisms with f|_Φ proper and f(Φ) ⊂ Ψ. For f between pure-dimensional X, Y of relative dimension r = dim X − dim Y there is a pushforward f_*: Ĥ((X, Φ)/S) → Ĥ((Y, Ψ)/S)(−r), where Ĥ((X, Φ)/S) = ⊕_{i,q} R^i(a_X)_Φ W Ω^q_X (a_X: X → S), the twist (−r) shifting the bidegree (q, i) to (q − r, i − r). It is defined from Ekedahl duality and the trace for the compactly supported direct image, makes (X, Φ) ↦ Ĥ((X, Φ)/S) a functor, commutes with F, V and d, is compatible with restriction to opens of S, and for open immersions is the excision isomorphism. For a finite morphism f: X → Y of connected smooth k-schemes, f_* ∘ f^* = deg(f) on W_•Ω_Y.
hypotheses: X, Y smooth over k (not necessarily proper); f proper on the supports.
The ˆ indicates the inverse limit over n of the de Rham–Witt systems.
proofSteps: Write K_X ≅ E(W_•ω_X)(N)[N] (WV.4/witt-canonical-system) and D_X = Hom(−, K_X). For f in Sm*/S, compose µ_X: E(W_•Ω_X) ≅ D_X(W_•Ω_X)(−N)[−N], the transformation θ_f: f_ΦD_X → Γ_ΨD_Y(f_*−) from the trace, D(f^*), and µ_Y^{−1}; this gives Rf_ΦW_•Ω_X → RΓ_ΨW_•Ω_Y(−r)[−r] and, after Ra_* and Rlim, f_*.
Functoriality and the compatibilities follow from those of θ_f and µ_X (CR12 Proposition 2.3.3).
f_*f^* = deg f for finite f: Gros's computation through the trace of finite flat morphisms (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/finite-locally-free-trace).
acceptance: For π: P¹ → Spec k, π_*: H¹(P¹, WΩ¹) → W(k) is the trace, an isomorphism.
For the Frobenius-twisted F_{X/k}: X → X^{(1)} of degree p^{dim X}, F_* F^* = p^{dim X}.

nodes.title: Cycle classes in Hodge–Witt cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: For X smooth over k and an integral closed subscheme Z ⊂ X of codimension c, Gros's cycle class ĉl(Z) ∈ H^c_Z(X, WΩ^c_X) is the image of the logarithmic cycle class cl_log(Z) ∈ H^c_Z(X_ét, W_•Ω^c_{X,log}) (the Gysin image of 1 on the smooth locus of Z, extended by purity). Extended linearly, these classes form the unique morphism of weak cohomology theories with supports from Chow groups with supports (CH_*, CH^*, ×, 1) to (PĤ_*, PĤ^*, T, e), where PĤ(X, Φ) = ⊕_p R^pΓ_Φ WΩ^p_X. In particular cycle classes are compatible with proper pushforward, flat and Gysin pullback, exterior products, ĉl(X) = 1, and ĉl of a divisor {0} ⊂ P¹ is c_1(O(1)).

proofSteps: Define cl_log by the Gysin isomorphism for smooth pairs and the purity isomorphism H^c_Z(X_ét, W_nΩ^c_log) ≅ H^c_{Z∖Z_sing}(X∖Z_sing, W_nΩ^c_log) (Gros), then map W_nΩ_log → W_nΩ.

nodes.title: The category of proper correspondences over a base
nodes.statement: Let S be a k-scheme. The category C_S has objects k-morphisms f: X → S with X smooth and quasi-projective over k; Hom_{C_S}(X, Y) := CH(X ×_k Y, P(X ×_S Y)), the Chow group with supports in the family P(X ×_S Y) of closed subsets of X ×_S Y that are proper over Y; composition is β ∘ α := p_{13*}(p_{12}^*α · p_{23}^*β) computed with Fulton's refined intersection product inside X × Y × Z with supports proper over Z. The identity of X is the diagonal Δ_X. If X and Y are proper over S, Hom_{C_S}(X, Y) = CH(X ×_S Y).

nodes.title: Correspondences supported in positive codimension kill WO-cohomology up to bounded torsion
nodes.statement: Let S be a k-scheme, X → S and Y → S in C_S, Z ⊂ X ×_S Y a closed subset proper over Y, and r ≥ 0. (i) If every point of Z maps to a point of codimension ≥ r in Y, there is N ≥ 1 with N · image(Ĥ([Z]/S)) ⊂ ⊕_{p ≥ r, q ≥ r} R^qg_*WΩ^p_Y. (ii) If X is equidimensional of dimension d and every point of Z maps to a point of codimension ≥ r in X, there is N ≥ 1 with N · ⊕_{p > d−r or q > d−r} R^qf_*WΩ^p_X ⊂ ker Ĥ([Z]/S). In particular, for r ≥ 1, a correspondence supported over a proper closed subset of Y (resp. of X) acts by a bounded-torsion map on ⊕_q R^qf_*WO_X (resp. on ⊕_q R^qf_*Wω_X).
hypotheses: Z proper over Y; N is the degree of a field extension coming from an alteration (N = 1 under resolution of singularities).
proofSteps: (i) Choose by an alteration (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem) a smooth equidimensional D of dimension dim Y − r with π: D → Y proper and π(D) ⊃ pr_2(Z), and Z_D ⊂ X ×_S D of the same dimension mapping onto Z; with N = [k(Z_D) : k(Z)], N·[Z] = [Γ_π] ∘ [Z_D] in C_S, so N·Ĥ([Z]/S) factors through π_*, which raises both p and q by r (WV.4/hodge-witt-pushforward).
(ii) Symmetrically N·[Z] = [Z_D] ∘ [Γ_π^t] with D → X of dimension d − r, and pullback to D kills degrees above d − r.
acceptance: On P¹ ×_k P¹ over S = Spec k, the cycle P¹ × {x} (supported over a point of the target, r = 1) has image in H¹(P¹, WΩ¹), so it acts by zero into H⁰(P¹, WO) (N = 1).
The cycle {x} × P¹ (supported over a point of the source) kills H¹(P¹, WO), H⁰(P¹, WΩ¹) and H¹(P¹, WΩ¹), but not H⁰(P¹, WO).

nodes.title: Finite quotients and topological finite quotients
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. A normal equidimensional k-scheme of finite type X is a finite quotient if there is a finite surjective morphism Y → X from a smooth k-scheme Y; a tame finite quotient if Y → X can be chosen of degree prime to p (as a locally constant function on Y); a topological finite quotient if there is a universal homeomorphism u: X → X′ onto a finite quotient X′. Equivalently (for X normal equidimensional) there is a universal homeomorphism X′ → X from a finite quotient X′. A universal homeomorphism u: X → Y of integral schemes with Y normal has degree p^n and factors the n-th relative Frobenius: there is v: Y → X^{(n)} with v ∘ u = F^n_{X/k} and (u × id) ∘ v = F^n_{Y/k}.
hypotheses: Universal homeomorphism = finite, surjective, radicial; between integral schemes with normal target this means finite surjective with purely inseparable function field extension.
proofSteps: A universal homeomorphism is finite, surjective and radicial, and for integral schemes with normal target this means finite surjective with purely inseparable function-field extension (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/universal-homeomorphism-criteria). Factorization of Frobenius: for X = Spec B, Y = Spec A affine, A ⊂ B with k(B)/k(A) purely inseparable of degree p^n; F^{n*}_{X/k} sends b ⊗ λ to b^{p^n}λ, and b^{p^n} ∈ k(A) ∩ B = A by normality of Y, giving v (CR12 Lemma 4.2.3; SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/relative-frobenius).
The equivalence of the two directions: X′^{(n)} is a finite quotient when X′ is, and Frobenius twists are isomorphisms of F_p-schemes since k is perfect (CR12 Remark 4.2.6).
acceptance: Every smooth k-scheme is a finite quotient.
A^n_k/G for a finite group G acting linearly is a finite quotient.

nodes.title: Quasi-resolutions
nodes.statement: A morphism f: X → Y between integral k-schemes is a quasi-resolution if its source X is a topological finite quotient, f is projective and surjective and finite over a dense open of Y, and the function-field extension k(Y) ⊂ k(X) is purely inseparable. Every integral k-scheme of finite type Y admits a quasi-resolution of the form X″/G → Y′ → Y, with Y′ → Y finite surjective and purely inseparable from a normal integral Y′, X″ smooth integral quasi-projective with a finite group G acting, and X″/G → Y′ projective birational. Any two quasi-resolutions of Y are dominated by a third. For X, Y integral normal, a projective surjective generically finite f factors as X → Y′ → Y through the normalization Y′ of Y in k(X), with X → Y′ birational and Y′ → Y finite, a universal homeomorphism when k(X)/k(Y) is purely inseparable.
hypotheses: k perfect; de Jong's alteration theorem in its equivariant form (Galois alterations) gives existence.
proofSteps: Existence: by de Jong (1997, Corollary 5.15; 1996, Corollary 7.4), a finite purely inseparable Y′ → Y with Y′ normal and a smooth quasi-projective X″ with G-action such that X″/G → Y′ is projective birational (Galois alterations: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII:PA.6/de-jong-galois-alteration over an algebraically closed field, with the perfect-field form requested from PA.6, gap CrystallineCohomologyPartII/G2; SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem); X″/G is a finite quotient, and the composite satisfies the definition (CR12 Remark 4.3.2).

Domination: given two quasi-resolutions, apply existence to the closure of the image of Spec L in X_1 ×_Y X_2, where L is the residue field of the local artinian algebra k(X_1) ⊗_{k(Y)} k(X_2) (purely inseparable over k(Y)).

acceptance: A resolution of singularities X → Y (projective birational with X smooth) is a quasi-resolution.

nodes.title: Finite covers and universal homeomorphisms realize Witt cohomology as a direct factor
nodes.statement: (i) For a universal homeomorphism u: X → Y between integral normal schemes, u_*u^* = deg(u) on WO_Y ⊕ Wω_Y and u^*u_* = deg(u) on u_*(WO_X ⊕ Wω_X); hence u^* and u_* are isomorphisms after passing to the isogeny category. (ii) Let f: X → Y be finite surjective with X smooth integral, Y, Z normal integral, u: Z → Y a universal homeomorphism and a: Y → S a morphism; put β = pr_{13*}[X ×_Y Z ×_Y X] ∈ Hom_{C_S}(X, X). Then f^* ∘ u_* induces isomorphisms R^i(au)_*(WO_Z ⊕ Wω_Z)_ℚ ≅ Ĥ(β/S)(R^i(af)_*(WO_X ⊕ Wω_X)_ℚ) for all i.
hypotheses: X smooth integral; Y, Z normal integral; pullback and pushforward on WO ⊕ Wω of normal schemes as in CR12 Definition 4.1.5.
proofSteps: (i) u_*u^* = deg u by the degree formula (WV.4/hodge-witt-pushforward); u^*u_* = deg u reduces, by Proposition 4.1.4 (4) (Witt canonical sheaves are determined in codimension one) to smooth X, Y, where u_* = Ĥ([Γ]/Y), u^* = Ĥ([Γ^t]/Y) and [Γ^t] ∘ [Γ] = [X ×_Y X] = deg u · [Δ_X] because u is flat and a homeomorphism.

(ii) Ĥ(β/Y) = f^*u_*u^*f_* as endomorphisms of f_*(WO_X ⊕ Wω_X) (reduce to smooth X, Y, Z by localization); by Proposition 3.5.10 its image after R^i(a)_* is the image of f^*u_*u^*f_*, and (u^*f_*)(f^*u_*) = deg f · deg u.
acceptance: For the Frobenius twist u = F_{X/k} of a smooth X, u_*u^* = p^{dim X} on WO_{X^{(1)}}.

nodes.title: Witt cohomology of a quasi-resolution of a topological finite quotient
nodes.statement: For a quasi-resolution f: X → Y of a topological finite quotient Y, pullback and pushforward give isomorphisms in the derived category of de Rham–Witt modules over Y up to isogeny: f^*: WO_{Y,ℚ} ≅ Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ} and Rf_*Wω_{X,ℚ} ≅ f_*Wω_{X,ℚ}[0] ≅ Wω_{Y,ℚ}. In particular R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = 0 and R^if_*Wω_{X,ℚ} = 0 for i ≥ 1: there is N with p^N R^if_*WO_X = 0 for all i ≥ 1.
hypotheses: Y a topological finite quotient (not just normal); f a quasi-resolution; isogeny convention.
proofSteps: Reduce to X, Y integral of dimension d and (by WV.5/finite-quotient-projector (i)) finite quotients, with finite surjective a: X′ → X, b: Y′ → Y from smooth integral schemes; factor f = u ∘ π with π projective birational onto a normal X_1 and u a universal homeomorphism; choose a dense smooth open U_0 ⊂ Y over which all maps are flat and π is an isomorphism.

With α = [X′ ×_X X′], β = [Y′ ×_Y Y′], γ = [X′ ×_Y Y′] in C_Y, the relations deg b·(γ∘α) − deg a·(β∘γ), deg a·(γ^t∘β) − deg b·(α∘γ^t), (γ^t∘γ∘α) − deg a·deg b·deg u·α and (γ∘γ^t∘β) − deg a·deg b·deg u·β hold up to cycles supported over Y ∖ U_0, by the localization sequence and [Γ_u]∘[Γ_u^t] = deg u·[Δ] over U_0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5/chow-localization).

By WV.4/correspondence-vanishing the error cycles act by bounded torsion, so Ĥ(γ/Y) and Ĥ(γ^t/Y) are inverse isomorphisms up to the nonzero integer deg a·deg b·deg u between the images of the projectors Ĥ(α/Y) and Ĥ(β/Y); WV.5/finite-quotient-projector (ii) identifies these images with R^if_*(WO_X ⊕ Wω_X)_ℚ and (WO_Y ⊕ Wω_Y)_ℚ, so the higher direct images vanish.

In degree 0: π^*: WO_{X_1} → π_*WO_X is an isomorphism (X_1 normal, π birational), and u^* is an isomorphism up to isogeny; for Wω, the pushforward is an isomorphism up to isogeny once f^* is (CR12 Lemma 4.3.4, via duality for W_nY).
acceptance: For the minimal resolution X → Y of the quadric cone A²/{±1} (p odd), R¹f_*WO_{X,ℚ} = 0; the exceptional curve is a P¹, consistent with WV.2/witt-exceptional-reduction (H¹(P¹, WO_ℚ) = 0).
For X smooth and f = F_{X/k}, the statement is the isogeny f_*f^* = p^{dim X}.

nodes.title: WO-rational and Witt-rational singularities
nodes.statement: An integral k-scheme S has Witt-rational singularities if for every quasi-resolution f: X → S: (1) f^*: WO_{S,ℚ} → f_*WO_{X,ℚ} is an isomorphism; (2) R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = 0 for all i ≥ 1; (3) R^if_*Wω_{X,ℚ} = 0 for all i ≥ 1. If only (1) and (2) hold, S has WO-rational singularities. Here the subscript ℚ is the isogeny convention: (2) means that a power of p kills R^if_*WO_X. Equivalently, it suffices that one quasi-resolution satisfies the conditions (one quasi-resolution suffices), and for normal S condition (1) is automatic; in particular, if S has a resolution of singularities, S is WO-rational iff R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = 0 for i > 0 for that resolution.
hypotheses: S integral of finite type over a perfect field k; the conditions are local on S.
BE-Witt-rational singularities (Blickle–Esnault: a splitting of WO_S ⊗ ℚ → Rf_*WO_X ⊗ ℚ for a generically étale alteration) are a weaker notion and are not used to define this one.
proofSteps: One quasi-resolution suffices: any two quasi-resolutions are dominated by a third (WV.5/quasi-resolution), and the dominating map between them is a quasi-resolution of a topological finite quotient, so WV.5/quasi-resolution-invariance and the Leray spectral sequence transfer the conditions (CR12 Proposition 4.4.6, with the analogue for WO).

For S normal, factor f = u ∘ π with π birational onto a normal X_1 and u a universal homeomorphism; π^* is an isomorphism on WO and u^* is one up to isogeny (WV.5/finite-quotient-projector (i)), giving (1) (CR12 Remark 4.4.5).
acceptance: Smooth schemes and topological finite quotients are Witt-rational (WV.5/finite-quotients-witt-rational).
The cone over a smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 1 is not WO-rational (WV.5/isolated-singularity-criterion).

nodes.title: Topological finite quotients are Witt-rational; invariance under universal homeomorphisms
nodes.statement: (i) Every topological finite quotient over k has Witt-rational singularities. (ii) If u: Y → Y′ is a universal homeomorphism between normal schemes, Y has Witt-rational (resp. WO-rational) singularities iff Y′ has.
hypotheses: k perfect; Y, Y′ normal integral in (ii).
proofSteps: (i) A topological finite quotient Y admits quasi-resolutions; WV.5/quasi-resolution-invariance gives (1)–(3) of WV.5/wo-rational-singularities for every quasi-resolution.
(ii) If f is a quasi-resolution of Y then u ∘ f is a quasi-resolution of Y′, and R^i(u∘f)_* = u_*R^if_* since u is finite; one quasi-resolution suffices (WV.5/wo-rational-singularities).

nodes.title: The Witt singularity complexes of an integral scheme
nodes.statement: Let S be an integral k-scheme of dimension d. For quasi-resolutions f: X → S and g: Y → S, X and Y are quasi-birational over S, and every quasi-birational correspondence (Z, π_X, π_Y) induces the same isomorphisms Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ Rg_*WO_{Y,ℚ} and Rf_*Wω_{X,ℚ} ≅ Rg_*Wω_{Y,ℚ} in the derived category of de Rham–Witt modules over S up to isogeny, compatibly with composition for three quasi-resolutions. Hence WS_{0,S} := Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ} and WS_{d,S} := Rf_*Wω_{X,ℚ} are well defined up to canonical isomorphism, with F and V, and S is WO-rational iff WO_{S,ℚ} → WS_{0,S} is an isomorphism, Witt-rational iff in addition H^i(WS_{d,S}) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
hypotheses: S integral of finite type over a perfect field.
Two integral S-schemes are quasi-birational over S if they admit quasi-resolutions from a common Z.
