nodes.title: Quasi-birational invariance of Witt cohomology for Witt-rational schemes
nodes.statement: Over a k-scheme S, take integral S-schemes f: X → S and g: Y → S, both with WO-rational singularities and quasi-birational over S. A quasi-birational correspondence induces Rf_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ Rg_*WO_{Y,ℚ} (and Rf_*Wω_{X,ℚ} ≅ Rg_*Wω_{Y,ℚ} when X, Y are Witt-rational), compatible with F and V. In particular, for S = Spec k: H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) ≅ H^i(Y, WO_{Y,ℚ}) for all i, and if X, Y are projective, H^i_rig(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^i_rig(Y/K)^{<1} Frobenius-equivariantly.
hypotheses: X, Y integral with WO-rational singularities, quasi-birational over S.
proofSteps: Given a quasi-birational correspondence (Z, π_X, π_Y), π_X and π_Y are quasi-resolutions and X, Y are WO-rational, so WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ Rπ_{X*}WO_{Z,ℚ} and similarly for Y; compose (CR12 Corollary 4.4.11, Remark 4.4.14).
For S = Spec k take cohomology; for projective X, Y apply WV.3/berthelot-bloch-esnault-comparison (proper case).
acceptance: A smooth projective X and its blowup along a smooth center have the same H^i(−, WO_ℚ).

sources.locator: Corollary 1 (introduction), p. 5; Corollary 4.4.11, Remark 4.4.14, Corollary 4.4.15 with proof, pp. 84–85
sources.match: Witt-rational (resp. WO-rational) quasi-birational schemes have isomorphic direct images of WO_ℚ (and Wω_ℚ); over k this identifies H^i(−, WO_ℚ) and, for projective schemes, the slope < 1 parts of rigid cohomology by BBE Theorem 1.1.

nodes.title: Rational singularities are Witt-rational
nodes.statement: For an integral k-scheme S: rational singularities (a resolution f with R^if_*O_X = 0 = R^if_*ω_X for i > 0) ⇒ Witt-rational ⇒ WO-rational ⇒ BE-Witt-rational (WO_S ⊗ ℚ → Rg_*WO_X ⊗ ℚ splits for every alteration g from a smooth scheme). The first implication is strict.
hypotheses: S integral of finite type over a perfect field; the first implication assumes a resolution exists (as part of the definition of rational singularities).
proofSteps: Rational ⇒ Witt-rational: from 0 → W_{n−1}O_X →(V) W_nO_X → O_X → 0 and R^if_*O_X = 0, R^if_*W_nO_X = 0 and W_nO_S ≅ f_*W_nO_X; with 0 → W_{n−1}ω_X →(p) W_nω_X → ω_X → 0 (WV.4/witt-canonical-system) and duality on the CM scheme S, the same for Wω; pass to the limit with WV.0/witt-limit-lemmas.

WO-rational ⇒ BE: choose a quasi-resolution by a finite quotient X with a smooth finite cover X′ → X; the pushforward splits the pullback up to the degree (WV.5/finite-quotient-projector), a fortiori after ⊗ℚ.
Strictness: WV.5/finite-quotients-witt-rational with the non-CM finite quotients of Ellingsrud–Skjelbred.
acceptance: A rational surface singularity (e.g. a du Val singularity in characteristic p with a rational resolution) is Witt-rational.

sources.locator: Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2, Proposition 4.4.3, Proposition 4.4.17 with proof, pp. 81–86
sources.match: Rational singularities and BE-Witt-rational singularities, and the chain of implications rational ⇒ Witt-rational ⇒ WO-rational ⇒ BE-Witt-rational, the first strict.

nodes.title: WO-rationality of isolated singularities through the exceptional fibre
nodes.statement: Let S be an integral normal k-scheme with an isolated singular point s and f: X → S a resolution of singularities that is an isomorphism over S ∖ {s}, with exceptional fibre E = f^{−1}(s). Then S has WO-rational singularities iff H^i(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) = 0 for all i > 0 (equivalently H^i(E, WO_E) ⊗ ℚ = 0, E being proper). In particular the cone over a smooth projective variety Z ⊂ P^N (with a resolution by the blowup of the vertex, E ≅ Z) is WO-rational iff H^i(Z, WO_{Z,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: S normal with an isolated singularity; a resolution that is an isomorphism away from s exists (an assumption).
proofSteps: WV.2/witt-exceptional-reduction gives R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = H^i(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) as skyscraper sheaves at s for i > 0; the resolution is a quasi-resolution and one suffices (WV.5/wo-rational-singularities); S is normal so condition (1) holds.
For E proper, the isogeny and tensor conventions agree on H^i (WV.0/rational-witt-sheaves).
acceptance: The cone over a smooth plane conic is WO-rational; the cone over a smooth plane curve of genus g ≥ 1 is not, since H¹(C, WO_C)_K, the slope-[0, 1) part of H¹_crys(C), has dimension ≥ g.
A normal surface singularity whose minimal resolution has exceptional curves forming a tree of smooth rational curves has H¹(E, WO_{E,ℚ}) = 0, by Mayer–Vietoris (WV.0/witt-closed-mayer-vietoris).

sources.match: For a projective birational f that is an isomorphism off an isolated singular point, R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} = H^i(E, WO_{E,ℚ}); hence S is WO-rational iff these vanish; a normal surface is WO-rational iff the exceptional divisor is a tree of smooth rational curves; a cone over a smooth projective X is WO-rational iff H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: Decomposition of the diagonal for CH_0-trivial varieties
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically integral variety of dimension d over a field k, and suppose CH_0(X_Ω) ⊗ ℚ = ℚ via the degree, where Ω is an algebraic closure of k(X). Then there are N ≥ 1, a zero-cycle ξ on X, a divisor D ⊂ X and a d-dimensional cycle Γ supported on X × D such that N·[Δ_X] = [ξ × X] + Γ in CH^d(X × X). More generally, for a smooth projective family X′_η over the generic point of a base, with CH_0 trivial over every field extension, the same holds for the generic fibre with N, D, ξ over η, which spreads out over a dense open of the base up to cycles supported over a divisor of the base.
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically integral; the CH_0 hypothesis over an algebraic closure of k(X) (or over every extension of the base field).
proofSteps: The kernel of CH_0(X_{k(X)}) → CH_0(X_Ω) is torsion: Ω is algebraic over k(X), so a class dying over Ω dies over a finite subextension k′ (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2/chow-groups-under-field-extension), and pushforward along the finite flat X_{k′} → X_{k(X)} after pullback is multiplication by [k′ : k(X)] (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5/finite-flat-degree).

Hence the generic point η_X ∈ X(k(X)) is, up to torsion, rationally equivalent over k(X) to a zero-cycle ξ_{k(X)} pulled back from X; CH_0(X_{k(X)}) is the colimit of CH^d(X × (X ∖ D)) over divisors D, so N(Δ − ξ × X) restricts to zero on X × (X ∖ D) for some D, and the localization sequence (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5/chow-localization) gives Γ on X × D.
The relative version: apply the same over the generic point of the base and spread out (CR12 proof of Theorem 4.8.1, (4.8.6)–(4.8.7)).
acceptance: For X = P^d: [Δ] = [pt × P^d] + Γ with Γ supported on P^d × H for a hyperplane H (N = 1).
For X an elliptic curve the hypothesis fails: CH_0(X_Ω) ⊗ ℚ ⊃ X(Ω) ⊗ ℚ is huge.

nodes.title: Vanishing of higher direct images of WO for fibrations with CH_0-trivial generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let X be an integral k-scheme with Witt-rational singularities and f: X → Y a projective morphism to an integral normal scheme Y, with generic point η and smooth generic fibre X_η, such that, for each field L containing k(η), degree identifies CH_0(X_η ×_{k(η)} L) with rational coefficients with ℚ. Then ⊕_{i>0} R^if_*WO_{X,ℚ} ≅ ⊕_{i>0} H^i(WS_{0,Y}) and ⊕_{i>0} R^if_*Wω_{X,ℚ} ≅ ⊕_{i>0} H^i(WS_{dim Y,Y}). When Y is itself Witt-rational, all these positive-degree direct images vanish; for Y = Spec k: H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: X Witt-rational (e.g. smooth); f projective; Y normal integral; X_η smooth; universal CH_0-triviality of X_η after ⊗ℚ.
proofSteps: Choose X′ → X′/G → X″ → X as in WV.5/quasi-resolution (X′ smooth, G finite acting, X″ → X a universal homeomorphism) and the Stein factorization Y″ → Y of X″ → Y, a universal homeomorphism.
The averaging correspondence P = ∑_{g∈G}[Γ(g)] on X′ ×_Y X′ realizes ⊕_{i>0} R^if_*(WO ⊕ Wω)_{X,ℚ} as the image of Ĥ(P/Y) (X is Witt-rational; CR12 Lemma 4.8.3; WV.5/finite-quotient-projector).

CH_0(X′_η ×_η L)^G ⊗ ℚ = ℚ for all L by push-pull along X′_η → X_η; WV.5/bloch-srinivas-decomposition gives N_1P + N_2[A_1] and M_1P + M_2[A_2] supported over divisors of X′ or over a divisor of Y, with A_1, A_2 the closures of α × X′_η and X′_η × α for a closed point α.

By WV.4/correspondence-vanishing, Ĥ(P/Y) acts as Ĥ([A_1]/Y) on ⊕_{i>0} R^if′_*WO_ℚ and as Ĥ([A_2]/Y) on the Wω part; an alteration of the closure of α (generically finite over Y) identifies these images with H^{>0}(WS_{0,Y}) and H^{>0}(WS_{dim Y,Y}) (CR12 Proposition 4.8.4, Theorem 4.5.6).
acceptance: For X = P^n_Y → Y with Y smooth, R^if_*WO_ℚ = 0 for i > 0.
For Y = Spec k and X a smooth projective rational (or rationally chain connected) variety, H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: The Witt zeta function and slope factors of the zeta function
nodes.statement: Let k = F_q, q = p^a, K = W(k)[1/p], and X a separated k-scheme of finite type with q-Frobenius φ = F^a (K-linear). Define P^W_i(X, t) := det(1 − tφ | H^i_c(X, WO_{X,K})) and ζ^W(X, t) := ∏_i P^W_i(X, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}}. With P_i(X, t) := det(1 − tφ | H^i_{rig,c}(X/K)), ζ(X, t) = ∏_i P_i(X, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}} (Lefschetz trace formula), and the slope < ρ factor ζ^{<ρ}(X, t) is defined through Newton polygons (WV.3/slope-subspace). The polynomials P^W_i(X, t) and the slope factors P^λ_i(X, t) lie in ℤ_p[t].
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over a finite field; v_q(q) = 1 for slopes.
proofSteps: H^i_c(X, WO_{X,K}) is finite-dimensional with slopes in [0, 1) (WV.2/compact-support-finiteness), so P^W_i is a polynomial with P^W_i(0) = 1 whose reciprocal roots have v_q in [0, 1).

P_i is invariant under σ (pullback along the absolute Frobenius of Spec k, and the relative Frobenius X → X′ induces an isomorphism on rigid cohomology), hence lies in ℚ_p[t]; the Newton-polygon factors are defined over ℚ_p; slopes are ≥ 0, so the reciprocal roots are p-adic integers and the factors lie in ℤ_p[t]; the same argument applies to P^W_i (BBE Proposition 6.2).
acceptance: ζ^W(Spec F_q, t) = 1/(1 − t).

The slope factors P^λ_i(X, t) and the Witt polynomials P^W_i(X, t) have coefficients in ℤ_p.

nodes.statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over F_q. For every i, P^{<1}_i(X, t) = P^W_i(X, t), and ζ^{<1}(X, t) = ζ^W(X, t).

proofSteps: By WV.3/berthelot-bloch-esnault-comparison, H^i_{rig,c}(X/K)^{<1} ≅ H^i_c(X, WO_{X,K}) compatibly with φ; by WV.3/slope-subspace (Manin) det(1 − tφ | E^{<1}) = det(1 − tφ | E)^{<1}; take the alternating product (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula).

nodes.title: Point counts modulo q^κ and slope factors (Ax)
nodes.statement: Let (N_r)_{r≥1} be integers with Φ(t) = exp(∑_{r≥1} N_r t^r/r) ∈ 1 + tℤ[[t]] a rational function in ℚ(t). Then Φ(t) = ∏_i(1 − α_it)/∏_j(1 − β_jt) with algebraic integers α_i ≠ β_j, and for every integer κ ≥ 1 the following are equivalent: (i) N_r ≡ 0 mod q^{κr} for all r ≥ 1; (ii) all α_i, β_j are divisible by q^κ in the ring of algebraic integers; (iii) v_q(ι(α_i)) ≥ κ and v_q(ι(β_j)) ≥ κ for every embedding ι: ℚ̄ → ℚ̄_p; (iv) Φ^{<κ}(t) = 1. In particular, for X, Y separated of finite type over F_q, ζ^{<1}(X, t) = ζ^{<1}(Y, t) iff |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ |Y(F_{q^r})| mod q^r for all r ≥ 1.
hypotheses: Φ rational with integer coefficients and constant term 1.
proofSteps: Fatou: a rational power series in 1 + tℤ[[t]] is a quotient of polynomials in 1 + tℤ[t] (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou), so the reciprocal roots and poles are algebraic integers, closed under Galois conjugation.

N_r = ∑_j β_j^r − ∑_i α_i^r; (ii) ⇒ (i) directly; (i) ⇒ (iii) by applying the q^{κr}-divisibility to the power sums and a Newton-polygon argument on the logarithmic derivative; (iii) ⇔ (iv) by the definition of the slope < κ factor; (iii) ⇒ (ii) since v_q ≥ κ at every embedding means divisibility by q^κ for algebraic integers.
The last assertion: apply to Φ = Z(X, t)/Z(Y, t) with N_r = |X(F_{q^r})| − |Y(F_{q^r})| and κ = 1 (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/closed-points-and-zeta-function).
acceptance: Φ(t) = 1/(1 − qt) (N_r = q^r) satisfies (i)–(iv) with κ = 1.
Φ(t) = 1/(1 − t) (N_r = 1) satisfies none of them.

sources.match: For integers N_r with rational Φ(t) = exp(∑ N_r t^r/r), divisibility of all N_r by q^{κr} is equivalent to the reciprocal zeros and poles being divisible by q^κ, to their q-adic valuations being ≥ κ at all embeddings, and to Φ^{<κ} = 1; attributed to Ax.

nodes.title: Isomorphisms on Witt cohomology give point-count congruences
nodes.statement: (i) Let f: X → Y be a proper morphism of separated F_q-schemes of finite type such that f^*: H^i_c(Y, WO_{Y,K}) → H^i_c(X, WO_{X,K}) is an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0. Then |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ |Y(F_{q^r})| mod q^r for all r ≥ 1. (ii) If f: X → Y is a morphism of proper F_q-schemes inducing isomorphisms H^i(Y, O_Y) ≅ H^i(X, O_X) for all i, then (i) applies: |X(F_q)| ≡ |Y(F_q)| mod q. (iii) If X is proper over F_q and G is a finite group acting on X with every orbit in an affine open, then H^i(X/G, WO_{X/G,K}) ≅ H^i(X, WO_{X,K})^G; if G acts trivially on H^i(X, WO_{X,K}) for all i (for instance, if |G| is prime to p and G acts trivially on H^i(X, O_X)), then |X(F_q)| ≡ |(X/G)(F_q)| mod q.
hypotheses: (i) f proper; (ii) X, Y proper; (iii) X proper with orbits in affine opens (so X/G exists).
proofSteps: (i) ζ^W(X) = ζ^W(Y) by the definition (WV.6/witt-zeta-function, Frobenius-equivariance of f^*), hence ζ^{<1}(X) = ζ^{<1}(Y) (WV.6/slope-zeta-identity), and WV.6/ax-congruence-criterion gives the congruences.

(ii) By induction on m with 0 → W_{m−1}O →(V) W_mO → O → 0 and the five lemma, H^i(Y, W_mO_Y) ≅ H^i(X, W_mO_X) for all m; for proper schemes H^i(−, WO) = lim_m H^i(−, W_mO) (WV.0/witt-sheaf), so the Witt cohomologies agree after ⊗K.

(iii) For the finite quotient map f: X → Y = X/G, O_Y = (f_*O_X)^G, R^if_*(W_mO_X) = 0 for i ≥ 1, W_mO_Y ≅ (f_*W_mO_X)^G; invariants commute with inverse limits and ⊗ℚ and, in characteristic 0, with cohomology (BBE Lemma 6.10). For |G| prime to p, invariants are exact on k[G]-modules, so H^i(Y, O_Y) = H^i(X, O_X)^G = H^i(X, O_X) and (ii) applies (BBE Corollary 6.12).
acceptance: For the Igusa surface Y = (E_1 × E_2)/(ℤ/2) with p = 2, G acts trivially on H^i(X, O_X) but not on H²(X, WO_K) ≠ 0 = H²(Y, WO_K): the hypothesis of (iii) on Witt cohomology cannot be replaced by one on O_X when p divides |G|.
The quotient of an abelian variety by a subgroup generated by a rational point of order p satisfies (iii) but not the hypothesis of (ii).

nodes.title: Point counts of schemes with WO-rational singularities
nodes.statement: Let X, Y be integral projective F_q-schemes with WO-rational singularities that are quasi-birational over F_q (for instance, Y → X a projective birational morphism, or a quasi-resolution, with Y WO-rational). Then |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ |Y(F_{q^r})| mod q^r for all r ≥ 1. In particular, if X has WO-rational singularities and f: Y → X is a resolution of singularities with Y projective (necessarily WO-rational), then |X(F_q)| ≡ |Y(F_q)| mod q.
hypotheses: X, Y projective and integral over a finite field; WO-rational singularities.
proofSteps: WV.5/quasi-birational-witt-invariance gives H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) ≅ H^i(Y, WO_{Y,ℚ}) Frobenius-equivariantly; for proper schemes the isogeny and tensor conventions agree on cohomology (WV.0/rational-witt-sheaves), so the Witt zeta functions agree; conclude with WV.6/slope-zeta-identity and WV.6/ax-congruence-criterion.
For a resolution f: Y → X with X WO-rational, Rf_*WO_{Y,ℚ} ≅ WO_{X,ℚ}, so f^* is an isomorphism on H^i(−, WO_K) and WV.6/witt-isomorphism-point-congruence (i) applies directly.
acceptance: The quadric cone X = A²/{±1}, compactified in P³ as a projective quadric cone, and its minimal resolution (a Hirzebruch surface F_2) have point counts congruent mod q: |X(F_q)| = q² + q + 1 and |F_2(F_q)| = (q + 1)², and both are ≡ 1 mod q.

sources.locator: Corollary 2 (introduction), p. 5; Corollary 4.4.16 with proof, p. 85
sources.match: Quasi-birational integral projective schemes with WO-rational singularities over a finite field have point counts congruent modulo |k′| over every finite extension k′, from Corollary 4.4.15 and BBE Corollary 1.3.
WO-rationality checked on one resolution holds for every resolution and every quasi-resolution.
For a WO-rational fourfold X and a resolution Y, GNT Remark 3.1 and BBE Proposition 6.9 give |X(F_q)| ≡ |Y(F_q)| mod q.

nodes.title: Witt cohomology of complete intersections of small degree and the Ax–Katz congruence modulo q
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and D_1, …, D_r ⊂ P^n_k hypersurfaces of degrees d_1, …, d_r with ∑_j d_j ≤ n, and Z = D_1 ∩ ⋯ ∩ D_r. Then H^0(Z, WO_{Z,K}) = K and H^i(Z, WO_{Z,K}) = 0 for i ≥ 1. Consequently, over k = F_q, ζ^{<1}(Z, t) = 1/(1 − t) and |Z(F_{q^s})| ≡ 1 mod q^s for all s ≥ 1 (Ax, Katz).
hypotheses: Hypersurfaces arbitrary (singular, reducible, nonreduced allowed); ∑ d_j ≤ n.
proofSteps: r = 1: for D of degree d ≤ n, H^i(P^n, O(−d)) = 0 for 0 ≤ i ≤ n (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/projective-space-cohomology), so H^i(P^n, O) ≅ H^i(D, O_D) for all i; by induction on m with the V-sequences, H^0(D, W_mO_D) = W_m(k) and H^i(D, W_mO_D) = 0 for i ≥ 1, hence the claim after the limit and ⊗K.

General r: D = D_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ D_r is a hypersurface of degree ∑ d_j ≤ n; the Mayer–Vietoris complex for the closed cover D = ∪ D_i (WV.0/witt-closed-mayer-vietoris) resolves WO_{Z,K} by WO-sheaves of D and of partial intersections, which by induction on r have the cohomology of a point, and the resulting complex of K's is exact except in degree 0.
Point counts: ζ^W(Z, t) = 1/(1 − t), so ζ^{<1}(Z, t) = 1/(1 − t) (WV.6/slope-zeta-identity), and WV.6/ax-congruence-criterion with Φ = ζ(Z, t)(1 − t) gives the congruences.
acceptance: A smooth plane conic (n = 2, d = 2) has q + 1 ≡ 1 mod q points.
A cubic surface in P³ (d = 3 ≤ 3) has |Z(F_q)| ≡ 1 mod q.

sources.locator: Corollary 1.5, p. 5; Proposition 6.8 with proof and proof of Corollary 1.5, pp. 37–38
sources.match: For hypersurfaces of total degree ≤ n in P^n, the intersection has the Witt vector cohomology of a point, hence ζ^{<1} = 1/(1 − t) and the number of rational points is ≡ 1 mod q, the best congruence obtainable from Witt cohomology toward Ax–Katz.

nodes.title: Slope < 1 zeta factor of an ample divisor with Witt-injective top cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety of pure dimension n over F_q and D ⊂ X an ample divisor with U = X ∖ D, such that (a) H^0(X, ω_X) → H^0(X, ω_X(D)) is an isomorphism and (b) for all i ≥ 1, V^i: H^n(X, O_X) → H^n(X, W_{i+1}O_X) is injective. Then the slope < 1 part of H^n_{rig,c}(U/K) maps isomorphically onto the slope < 1 part of H^n_rig(X/K), and the slope < 1 zeta factor of X is that of D multiplied by P^{<1}_n(X, t)^{(−1)^{n+1}}.
hypotheses: X smooth projective of pure dimension n over F_q; D ample (so U is affine); hypotheses (a), (b).
proofSteps: With I = O_X(−D), (a) is equivalent by Serre duality (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/cm-serre-duality) to H^n(X, I) ≅ H^n(X, O_X); with (b) the rows 0 → H^n(X, I) → H^n(X, W_{i+1}I) → H^n(X, W_iI) → 0 and the same for O_X are exact, so H^n(X, W_iI) ≅ H^n(X, W_iO_X) for all i, giving H^n_c(U, WO_{U,K}) ≅ H^n(X, WO_{X,K}) after the limit and ⊗K.

WV.3/berthelot-bloch-esnault-comparison transfers this to rigid cohomology; U is smooth affine of pure dimension n, so H^i_c(U, WO_K) = 0 for i ≠ n (WV.3/affine-witt-vanishing); by WV.6/slope-zeta-identity, ζ^{<1}(U, t) = P^W_n(U, t)^{(−1)^{n+1}} = P^{<1}_n(X, t)^{(−1)^{n+1}}; multiplicativity ζ(X) = ζ(U)ζ(D) gives the formula.
acceptance: For X = P¹ and D a k-point, (a) holds (both sides 0) and (b) is vacuous (H¹(P¹, O) = 0); the formula reads 1/(1 − t) = 1/(1 − t) · 1.

sources.match: Under (a) and (b), the compactly supported Witt cohomology of the affine complement equals H^n(X, WO_{X,K}), which gives the identity of slope < 1 zeta factors via Corollaries 1.2 and 1.3.

nodes.title: Theta divisors have congruent point counts modulo q
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over F_q and Θ, Θ′ two theta divisors on A (effective divisors with O_A(Θ) ample defining a principal polarization). Then |Θ(F_{q^r})| ≡ |Θ′(F_{q^r})| mod q^r for all r ≥ 1; in particular |Θ(F_q)| ≡ |Θ′(F_q)| mod q.
hypotheses: A abelian variety over a finite field; Θ, Θ′ theta divisors (not necessarily algebraically equivalent translates).
proofSteps: Check the hypotheses of WV.6/theta-divisor-criterion for (A, Θ): ω_A ≅ O_A and h^0(A, O_A(Θ)) = 1 for a principal polarization (Riemann–Roch on abelian varieties, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2/ample-cohomology-and-degree), so H^0(A, O_A) → H^0(A, O_A(Θ)) is an isomorphism, giving (a).
(b) is Serre's vanishing of Bockstein operations on abelian varieties: V^i: H^g(A, O_A) → H^g(A, W_{i+1}O_A) is injective for all i (requested from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2).
Hence ζ^{<1}(Θ, t) = ζ^{<1}(A, t)·P^{<1}_g(A, t)^{(−1)^g} = ζ^{<1}(Θ′, t), and WV.6/ax-congruence-criterion gives the congruences.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E (g = 1) a theta divisor is a single rational point, and the statement is 1 ≡ 1.
Two theta divisors differing by translation by a rational point have equal point counts; the theorem covers divisors that are not translates.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 5; 6.5 (proof of Theorem 1.4) and Remarks 6.6, pp. 36–37
sources.match: Two theta divisors on an abelian variety over F_q have the same number of rational points mod q, answering a question of Serre; the proof verifies the hypotheses of Proposition 6.4 using h^0(O(Θ)) = 1 and Serre's vanishing of Bocksteins for abelian varieties.

nodes.title: Universally CH_0-trivial varieties
nodes.statement: A proper k-scheme X is universally CH_0-trivial (rationally) if for every field extension L ⊃ k the degree map deg: CH_0(X_L) ⊗ ℚ → ℚ is an isomorphism. It suffices to check algebraically closed L ⊃ k. For X smooth projective geometrically integral, universal CH_0-triviality gives a decomposition of the diagonal N[Δ_X] = [ξ × X] + Γ with Γ supported on X × D for a divisor D (WV.5/bloch-srinivas-decomposition). For a family f: X → Y, the condition is imposed on the generic fibre over k(η).
hypotheses: Rational coefficients; X proper so that deg is defined.

Esnault's hypothesis (CH_0(X_Ω) = ℤ for Ω an algebraic closure of k(X) only) implies universal triviality through the decomposition of the diagonal and the moving lemma for zero-cycles; that implication is not used in this roadmap, whose theorems assume universal triviality.
proofSteps: Reduction to algebraically closed L: for any L, let L̄ be an algebraic closure; a class in the kernel of CH_0(X_L) → CH_0(X_{L̄}) dies over a finite subextension L′/L (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2/chow-groups-under-field-extension), and pushforward along the finite flat X_{L′} → X_L after pullback is multiplication by [L′ : L] (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5/finite-flat-degree), so the kernel is torsion; deg is surjective after ⊗ℚ because X_L has a zero-cycle of positive degree.
The decomposition of the diagonal is WV.5/bloch-srinivas-decomposition applied with Ω an algebraic closure of k(X), an algebraically closed extension of k.
acceptance: P^n is universally CH_0-trivial.

sources.match: Its hypothesis on the generic fibre: degree identifies CH_0 after any extension of k(η), with rational coefficients, with ℚ.
The hypothesis CH_0(X ×_k \overline{k(X)}) = ℤ, the norm argument for the kernel over the algebraic closure, and the decomposition of the diagonal it implies.

hypothesis for the vanishing of the slope [0, 1) part of H^i, i > 0
the hypothesis of the theorem

nodes.title: Rationally chain connected varieties
nodes.statement: A k-scheme X of finite type is rationally chain connected if there are a k-variety Y, a family g: U → Y of geometrically connected proper algebraic curves whose geometric fibres have only rational components, and a cycle morphism u: U → X such that u^{(2)}: U ×_Y U → X ×_k X is dominant. This property is invariant under field extension: X is rationally chain connected iff X ×_k k′ is, for any extension k′/k. Over an uncountable algebraically closed field, X is rationally chain connected iff a pair of general closed points can be joined by a chain of rational curves.
hypotheses: X of finite type over a field k; the family of curves is a 'cycle-theoretic' family in Kollár's sense.
proofSteps: Families of proper curves are parametrized by Hilbert schemes or Chow varieties (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/hilbert-scheme). Invariance under field extension and the characterization over uncountable algebraically closed fields are Kollár, Rational curves on algebraic varieties, IV.3.2.5 and IV.3.6, recorded in GNT Remark 4.6 (with Tanaka's Proposition A.4 for the field-extension statement); Kollár's book was not read for this plan (CrystallineCohomologyPartII/G1).
acceptance: P^n and smooth cubic surfaces are rationally chain connected.

sources.match: Defines rational chain connectedness by a family of proper connected curves with rational geometric fibre components and a dominant u^{(2)}, after Kollár IV.3.2, and records invariance under field extension and the characterization by chains through general points over uncountable algebraically closed fields.
Fano varieties over algebraically closed fields are chain rationally connected (Kollár V.2.13), which implies CH_0 = ℤ over the algebraic closure of the function field.
The point-count corollary assumes a rationally chain connected log resolution, with the definition of GNT Definition 4.5.

nodes.title: Rationally chain connected smooth projective varieties are universally CH_0-trivial
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over a field k that is rationally chain connected. Then X is universally CH_0-trivial: for every field extension L ⊃ k, deg: CH_0(X_L) ⊗ ℚ → ℚ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically connected and rationally chain connected.
proofSteps: By WV.6/universal-chow-zero-triviality it suffices to treat algebraically closed L ⊃ k; X_L is rationally chain connected by invariance under field extension (WV.6/rationally-chain-connected).

For a proper rationally chain connected scheme over an algebraically closed field, any two closed points are joined by a chain of rational curves, and two points of a rational curve are rationally equivalent (the normalization is P¹, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5/rational-equivalence), so every closed point is rationally equivalent to a fixed one and deg: CH_0(X_L) → ℤ is an isomorphism (Kollár IV.3.13.3; not read, CrystallineCohomologyPartII/G1).
acceptance: Smooth Fano varieties over algebraically closed fields are rationally chain connected (Kollár V.2.13), hence universally CH_0-trivial.

sources.match: Chain rational connectedness over the algebraic closure of k(X) implies CH_0(X ×_k \overline{k(X)}) = ℤ, citing Kollár's book.
Invariance of rational chain connectedness under field extension and the chain characterization over uncountable algebraically closed fields.

nodes.title: Vanishing of Witt vector cohomology of universally CH_0-trivial varieties
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically integral variety over a perfect field k of characteristic p that is universally CH_0-trivial (for instance, rationally chain connected). Then H^i(X, WO_X) ⊗ ℚ = 0 for all i > 0; equivalently, all Frobenius slopes of H^i_crys(X/W(k)) ⊗ ℚ (= H^i_rig(X/K)) are ≥ 1 for i > 0.
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically integral over a perfect field; universal CH_0-triviality (rational coefficients).
proofSteps: X is smooth, hence Witt-rational (WV.5/finite-quotients-witt-rational); apply WV.5/chow-trivial-fibration-vanishing to f: X → Spec k (Y = Spec k smooth, so WS_{0,k} = W(k)_ℚ has no higher cohomology): H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0, and for proper X this is H^i(X, WO_X) ⊗ ℚ = 0 (WV.0/rational-witt-sheaves).
Equivalence with the slope statement: H^i(X, WO_X)_K is the slope-[0, 1) part of H^i_crys(X/W)_K (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/witt-slope-spectral-sequence; WV.3/smooth-proper-slope-identification).

Esnault's original route (cycle classes in rigid cohomology acting by correspondences, with Berthelot's lemma that cohomology with supports in a divisor has slopes ≥ 1) is not planned here; the correspondence action of WV.4 replaces it.
acceptance: For X = P^n: H^i(P^n, WO) = 0 for i > 0 and H^{2j}_crys has slope j.
For a smooth cubic surface: all slopes of H²_crys equal 1.

sources.match: For smooth projective X over a perfect field with CH_0 trivial over the algebraic closure of the function field, the slope [0, 1) part of H^i(X/K) vanishes for i > 0, proved by Bloch's decomposition of the diagonal and Berthelot's lemma on slopes of cohomology with supports.
The relative Witt-vector statement, which for Y = Spec k gives the vanishing of H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) for i > 0.

Uses Esnault Theorem 1.1 for the rationally chain connected resolution: all slopes of Frobenius in positive degrees are ≥ 1 (PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/E11 restricts the printed assertion to positive degrees).

nodes.title: Rational points of universally CH_0-trivial varieties and of their WO-rational degenerations
nodes.statement: (i) Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_q that is universally CH_0-trivial (for instance, rationally chain connected, or Fano). Then |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ 1 mod q^r for all r ≥ 1; in particular X has an F_q-rational point. (ii) Let X be a projective geometrically connected F_q-scheme with WO-rational singularities that admits a resolution of singularities f: Y → X (or a quasi-resolution from a Witt-rational Y) with Y smooth projective, geometrically connected and universally CH_0-trivial. Then |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ 1 mod q^r for all r ≥ 1.
hypotheses: (i) X smooth projective geometrically connected; (ii) X with WO-rational singularities and such a resolution.
proofSteps: (i) H^0(X, WO_{X,K}) = K (geometric connectedness, X proper) and H^i(X, WO_{X,K}) = 0 for i > 0 (WV.6/esnault-witt-vanishing), so ζ^W(X, t) = 1/(1 − t) = ζ^{<1}(X, t) (WV.6/slope-zeta-identity); apply WV.6/ax-congruence-criterion to Φ = ζ(X, t)(1 − t).
(ii) WV.6/witt-rational-point-congruence gives |X(F_{q^r})| ≡ |Y(F_{q^r})| mod q^r, and (i) for Y.
acceptance: A smooth cubic surface over F_q has ≡ 1 mod q points.
Projective space: |P^n(F_q)| = 1 + q + ⋯ + q^n ≡ 1 mod q.

sources.match: Smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over F_q with trivial CH_0 over the algebraic closure of the function field, in particular Fano or chain rationally connected ones, have a rational point; the congruence 1 mod q follows from the trace formula when all slopes in positive degrees are ≥ 1.

A four-dimensional Q-factorial klt variety over F_q (p > 5) with a rationally chain connected log resolution has |X(F_q)| ≡ 1 mod q, by WO-rationality, GNT Remark 3.1, BBE Proposition 6.9 and Esnault; this roadmap supplies the cohomological part (ii), and the birational part (WO-rationality of klt fourfolds) belongs to the birational geometry roadmap.
The threefold analogue: Fano-type threefolds over F_q (p > 5) have ≡ 1 mod q points, via H^i(X, WO_{X,ℚ}) = 0 for i > 0.

requests.need: Serre's vanishing of Bockstein operations for abelian varieties: for an abelian variety A of dimension g over a perfect field k of characteristic p and every i ≥ 1, the map V^i: H^g(A, O_A) → H^g(A, W_{i+1}O_A) is injective (equivalently the boundary H^{g−1}(A, W_iO_A) → H^g(A, O_A) of 0 → O_A →(V^i) W_{i+1}O_A → W_iO_A → 0 vanishes). Source: J.-P. Serre, 'Quelques propriétés des variétés abéliennes en caractéristique p', Amer. J. Math. 80 (1958), Théorème 2, and 'Sur la topologie des variétés algébriques en caractéristique p' (1958), §§1, 3, as cited in Berthelot–Bloch–Esnault §6.5. The Witt sheaves are those of CrystallineCohomologyPartII:WV.0/witt-sheaf.

de Jong's Galois alterations over a perfect field (not only an algebraically closed one), in the form used for quasi-resolutions: for an integral separated scheme Y of finite type over a perfect field k there are a finite surjective purely inseparable Y′ → Y with Y′ normal and integral, a smooth integral quasi-projective X″ over k with a finite group G acting on it, and a projective birational morphism X″/G → Y′ (de Jong, 'Families of curves and alterations', Ann. Inst. Fourier 47 (1997), Corollary 5.15; 'Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations' (1996), Corollary 7.4). PA.6/de-jong-galois-alteration states the equivariant theorem over algebraically closed k.

remaining: BBE leave the compatibilities of a_U with reduction and excision (Proposition 4.6) as exercises; the plan records them as API of WV.3/rigid-to-witt-morphism with the Čech-functoriality argument, to be written out at lemma level.

Ekedahl's duality theorems for the de Rham–Witt complex of smooth schemes and Gros's cycle class are used through the statements recorded in Chatzistamatiou–Rülling §§1.10 and 3.2; refine WV.4/witt-canonical-system and WV.4/hodge-witt-cycle-class against Ekedahl (Ark. Mat. 22, 1984; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse 1985) and Gros (Mém. SMF 21, 1985) at lemma level.
Gap CrystallineCohomologyPartII/G2 and the request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII:PA.6: de Jong's Galois alterations over a perfect field for the existence of quasi-resolutions.
Request to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2 for Serre's vanishing of Bocksteins on abelian varieties (theta-divisor congruence).
Gap CrystallineCohomologyPartII/G1: Kollár's results on rational chain connectedness (base change, chains, CH_0) were not read.

gaps.title: Rational chain connectedness: base change and CH_0 (Kollár's book not read)
gaps.detail: The invariance of rational chain connectedness under field extension (Kollár, Rational curves on algebraic varieties, IV.3.2.5; Tanaka, Proposition A.4), the characterization through chains of rational curves joining general points over uncountable algebraically closed fields (Kollár IV.3.6), and the consequence CH_0(X_Ω) = ℤ for proper RCC X over algebraically closed Ω (Kollár IV.3.13.3) are recorded from Gongyo–Nakamura–Tanaka Remark 4.6 and Esnault 2003 §1, which cite them. Kollár's book is neither freely available nor in the cleared library, so the proofs were not read; the statements are planned as targets with these locators.

gaps.title: Galois alterations over perfect fields for quasi-resolutions
gaps.detail: Existence of quasi-resolutions over a perfect field k uses de Jong 1997 Corollary 5.15 (and 1996 Corollary 7.4) as recorded in Chatzistamatiou–Rülling Remark 4.3.2. The atlas supplier AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII:PA.6/de-jong-galois-alteration states the equivariant alteration theorem over an algebraically closed field; the perfect-field form (with a purely inseparable finite Y′ → Y) is requested from PA.6. de Jong's papers were not read for this plan.

sourceIssues.reason: I ⊂ O_X and Zeros(I) ⊂ X in the same sentence; the proof applies BBE Theorem 2.4, where the ideal on the source is the pullback of an ideal on the target.

restructure.detail: The design job for CrystallineCohomologyPartII (issue #3444) received four Part II routes of CrystallineCohomology. Two of them share their object and are planned here as one roadmap: Bhatt–Scholze 2017 §11.5 (h-descent of Frobenius-inverted Witt vector cohomology, route CrystallineCohomologyWittHDescentPartII, 3 items) and Hacon–Witaszek 2023 (rational Witt vector cohomology of singular schemes, route CrystallineCohomologySingularWittRationality, 5 items: witt-uh → WV.0/witt-universal-homeomorphism-invariance, witt-ideal → WV.2/witt-ideal-vanishing and WV.2/witt-exceptional-reduction, witt-low-slopes → WV.3/berthelot-bloch-esnault-comparison, one-quasi-resolution → WV.5/wo-rational-singularities, rcc-witt → WV.6/esnault-witt-vanishing). The other two are independent directions that share only the interfaces CR.1, CR.5 and CR.7: Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin 2022 Appendix A (log enlargements, convergent log F-isocrystals and the tensor-section extension over semi-abelian degenerations, 22 items) and Esnault–Groechenig 2020 (p-curvature, the crystalline differential operators and their Azumaya property, Ogus–Vologodsky, Higgs–de Rham flows and rigid connections, 63 items). Combining them would join unrelated carriers in one roadmap.

Neither (a) nor (b) depends on this roadmap or it on them.

upstreamNotes.note: §0.26 defines the Witt scheme W_nX only for perfect F_p-schemes (wittScheme n X with W_n(Spec A) = Spec W_n(A)). Witt vector cohomology of singular varieties needs W_nX = (|X|, W_nO_X) for arbitrary F_p-schemes of finite type (the quasi-coherent Witt ideal sheaves W_nI live on it); CrystallineCohomologyPartII:WV.0/witt-sheaf plans the general construction and states its agreement with §0.26 for perfect X. §0.26's frobenius_factors_through_universalHomeomorphism is the input used for invariance of Frobenius-inverted Witt cohomology.
